Current CPR/First Aid certification (American Heart Association or American Red Cross), annual negative TB screening, and a valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record and reliable transportation.
• Experience: Minimum of five years of nursing experience supporting individuals with Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities (IDD), including at least two years of supervisory experience. Experience supporting licensed IDD, ICF/IID, group home, or similarly regulated residential healthcare environments is strongly preferred.
• Clinical Expertise: Demonstrated knowledge of medication administration, RN delegation, aspiration risk management, seizure protocols, behavioral health integration, infection prevention and control, wound care, chronic disease management, and person-centered healthcare practices.
• Regulatory & Compliance Knowledge: Working knowledge of federal and Indiana regulations governing ICF/IID services, Indiana Medicaid Waiver programs, HIPAA/HITECH privacy requirements, BDDS and IDOH incident reporting processes, Adult Protective Services reporting requirements, and other applicable state and federal healthcare regulations.
• Leadership & Operational Management: Demonstrated ability to lead and develop nursing teams, oversee quality assurance initiatives, manage nursing operating budgets, staffing models, and cost-benefit analyses while ensuring high-quality clinical outcomes.
• Training & Education: Ability and willingness to teach state-required Med Core A & B training and routinely proctor training to ensure staff competency and consistent, high-quality delivery.
• Technical Skills: Proficiency with Microsoft 365 applications including Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams, and SharePoint, along with electronic health record (EHR) or clinical documentation platforms such as Therap.

NICE TO HAVE:

• Education: minimum associate's degree in nursing, preferred
• Industry Expertise: Experience leading nursing services across multiple IDD, ICF/IID, residential, or community-based healthcare programs.
• Leadership Development: Experience mentoring clinical leaders, developing nursing education programs, and leading organizational or process improvement initiatives.
• Quality & Compliance: Experience with clinical auditing, survey readiness, corrective action planning, incident management, and continuous quality improvement programs.
• Technology & Clinical Systems: Experience utilizing electronic health records, workforce management systems, and clinical reporting tools to improve operational efficiency and healthcare outcomes.

SKILLS CRITICAL FOR SUCCESS:

• Clinical Leadership & Team Development: You inspire, mentor, and develop nursing professionals while fostering accountability, collaboration, and exceptional clinical care.

• Strategic Thinking & Problem Solving: You proactively identify clinical risks, evaluate complex situations, and implement solutions that improve healthcare outcomes.
• Organization & Operational Excellence: You successfully balance multiple priorities while maintaining compliance, quality standards, and efficient nursing operations.
• Regulatory & Quality Focus: You have a strong commitment to regulatory compliance, quality assurance, and continuous improvement that ensure exceptional care for the individuals we serve.
• Adaptability & Accountability: You remain calm under pressure, confidently lead through change, and take ownership of organizational and clinical outcomes.

WHY YOU’LL LOVE THIS JOB:

As Director of Nursing, you'll have the opportunity to shape the future of clinical care across our Indiana operations while making a lasting impact on the lives of individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities. You'll serve as a trusted leader, partnering with executive leadership, mentoring nursing professionals, and driving initiatives that improve quality, compliance, and healthcare outcomes.

Performs clinical, educational and research responsibilities within the Infection Prevention Department, working in collaboration with and reporting to the Manager and the Medical Directors of Healthcare Epidemiology and Infection Prevention (HEIP) to reduce the risk of healthcare associated infection and to ensure the safety and health of all patients, visitors and personnel.

• Ensures compliance with regulatory and accreditation agencies, including the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid (CMS), Illinois, Chicago and Cook County Departments of Public Health, and The Joint Commission, as well as recommendations of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).
• Performs surveillance rounds on designated units and high risk areas.
• Collects and analyzes infection information for both patients and healthcare personnel.
• Serves as a leader/mentor and subject matter expert to staff in the areas related to infection prevention.

• Presents the findings of surveillance data and special investigations/studies to the appropriate individuals and the Committee on Infection Control and Prevention (CIC).
• Collaborates with Corporate Health in all areas relating to staff issues involving infectious disease exposures.
• Completes and submits reportable data to local, state, and national agencies.
• Presents lectures, orientation and training related to infection prevention.
• Conducts compliance monitoring for hand hygiene and adherence to established policy to assure patient and staff safety.
• Participates in Environment of Care (EOC) rounds and provides recommendations for remediation when necessary.

• Surveillance indicators as outlined in the Risk Assessment and Infection Prevention Plan are reported as required to the appropriate agencies.

Required:

jobs.title: Senior Principal Inbound Product Manager, CRM Voice AI
jobs.description:
About the Team:

CRM Voice AI builds autonomous voice agents for customer service that resolve customer interactions end-to-end and drive significant value for the business. We're a team inside ServiceNow's CRM business unit, shipping production voice AI with enterprise customers today and scaling aggressively. Our agents run on a real-time streaming voice pipeline with best-in-class orchestration, integrated into the same platform where many of our customers already manage their front, middle, and back-office workflows. For those that don't, the voice agent is often the tip of the spear that brings them in. We compete directly against well-funded AI startups and CCaaS incumbents, and we're winning.

How We Work:

We work in pods - small, dedicated teams embedded with a single enterprise customer, building their voice agents from first call to self-sufficiency. A pod owns the full lifecycle: agent shadowing, conversation design, build, production go-live, monitoring and optimization and the handoff that makes the customer self-sufficient so the pod can move on to the next one. Each pod pairs forward-deployed engineers with a product manager who owns both the customer outcome and the product learning that comes from it.

Every PM on this team runs at least one pod directly and has visibility across others. You're in the customer's world - on their calls, in their systems, solving their problems - while simultaneously shaping what the product becomes. The learnings from your pods feed directly into the platform roadmap and into repeatable, productized assets that scale beyond any single customer.

What This Role Owns:

• You run one pod directly - one of our most complex customer engagements - and float across two others, providing product direction and unblocking teams. You own the relationship with the customer’s leadership team – setting the timelines and expectations, then delivering on them.
• For those pods, you and your team of FDEs own agent design, the build and evaluation.
• You drive ServiceNow’s conversational experience itself: dialog quality, turn-taking, interruption handling, barge-in behavior, and endpointing. You collaborate directly with the platform voice team on voice pipeline innovation, the low-latency infrastructure that makes a voice agent feel like a conversation rather than a bot reading a script. When the platform team is making stack decisions about real-time streaming, LLM orchestration, or voice-to-voice model integration, you're in the room with production customer data and real-world edge cases.
• You will support customers across our industry verticals. As we scale across customers, you evaluate which patterns, intents, and conversation flows can be productized into out-of-the-box voice content for a specific industry. You're turning one-off wins into repeatable assets, and you have the customer exposure to know which abstractions actually hold.

Why This and Not Somewhere Else:

You're not choosing between startup speed and enterprise scale. You get both. This team ships voice AI in production with real enterprise customers, with the same urgency and ownership you'd find at a startup, backed by a platform that supports 85% of the Fortune 500. You have a direct seat at the platform table, influencing voice infrastructure decisions with data from your own deployments. This role puts you in a customer's contact center debugging a live voice agent one day and shaping platform architecture decisions the next. That combination is rare, and it's why this team exists.

What You Bring:

• 12+ years of product management experience, with recent hands-on work shipping voice AI or conversational AI products. What you've shipped in the last 12-18 months matters more than total years.
• Hands-on experience building and evaluating AI agents - conversation design, prompt engineering, testing and iteration against real user interactions. This is the core of the job; the voice stack expertise below layers on top of it.
• Fluency with the voice stack: ASR, TTS, streaming pipelines, latency optimization, endpointing, barge-in, turn-taking. You've made real tradeoff decisions here, not just evaluated vendor demos.
• Experience with telephony integration: SIP, call transfers, IVR systems, or CCaaS platforms.
• Experience working directly with enterprise customers on technical deployments - not from a distance, but in their environment, on their calls, solving their problems.
• Strong opinions on what makes a voice conversation feel human, backed by experience building or evaluating conversational systems.
• Technical depth in LLM orchestration for real-time conversational use cases.
• Experience defining voice-specific evaluations such as task completion, latency, transcription accuracy, and conversational quality.

Even Better:

• A track record of productizing customer-specific solutions into repeatable, industry-level assets.
• Industry expertise in verticals with high contact center volume: telecommunications, financial services, travel, healthcare.

jobs.title: Principal Inbound Product Manager, CRM Voice AI
jobs.description:
About the Team:

CRM Voice AI builds autonomous voice agents for customer service that resolve customer interactions end-to-end and drive significant value for the business. We're a team inside ServiceNow's CRM business unit, shipping production voice AI with enterprise customers today and scaling aggressively. Our agents run on a real-time streaming pipeline with best-in-class orchestration, integrated into the same platform where many of our customers already manage their front, middle, and back-office workflows. For those that don't, the voice agent is often the tip of the spear that brings them in. We compete directly against well-funded AI startups and CCaaS incumbents, and we're winning.

How We Work:

We work in pods - small, dedicated teams embedded with a single enterprise customer, building their voice agents from first call to self-sufficiency. A pod owns the full lifecycle: agent shadowing, conversation design, build, production go-live, monitoring and optimization and the handoff that makes the customer self-sufficient so the pod can move on to the next one. Each pod pairs forward-deployed engineers with a product manager who owns both the customer outcome and the product learning that comes from it.

Every PM on this team runs at least one pod directly and has visibility across others. You're in the customer's world - on their calls, in their systems, solving their problems - while simultaneously shaping what the product becomes. The learnings from your pods feed directly into the platform roadmap and into repeatable, productized assets that scale beyond any single customer.

What This Role Owns:

• You run one pod directly and float across one to two others, providing product direction and unblocking teams. You own the relationship with the customer’s leadership team, setting the timelines and expectations, then delivering on them.
• For those pods, you and your team of FDEs own agent design, the build and evaluation.
• Beyond your pods, you own STT and TTS model evaluation and experimentation for CRM Voice AI. The speech model landscape is moving fast. New ASR and TTS models ship constantly, each with different tradeoffs on latency, accuracy, naturalness, language support, and cost. You run structured evaluations against real production workloads, collaborate closely with the platform voice team on model decisions, and drive experimentation across our customer base. When a new model drops and the question is "should we move our customers to this?" - you're the one with the methodology, the data, and the production context to answer it.
• You also support a variety of industry verticals. As you see patterns across your pods and model evaluations, you identify which capabilities and conversation designs can be prioritized and productized for a specific industry, building the playbook for how CRM Voice AI enters a new market.

Why This and Not Somewhere Else:

The pod model means you’ll accumulate more production voice AI experience in a year than most PMs get in several - building agents across different industries, different contact center environments, and different conversation types. On top of that, speech models are the most dynamic layer of the voice AI stack right now, and most PMs evaluating them do it in a lab. You're doing it against real production traffic with enterprise customers who have real SLAs. You sit at the intersection of the platform team building the voice infrastructure and the CRM team deploying it, with influence in both directions. The right evaluation methodology is a genuine competitive advantage, and you're the person building it.

What You Bring:

• 8+ years of product management experience, with recent work in voice AI, conversational AI, or speech technology.
• Hands-on experience building and evaluating AI agents - conversation design, prompt engineering, testing and iteration against real user interactions. This is the foundation; speech model expertise layers on top of it.
• Working knowledge of speech models - ASR architectures, TTS synthesis approaches, and the tradeoffs between latency, accuracy, naturalness, and cost. You've evaluated or deployed these in production, not just prototyped.
• Comfort with experimentation and evaluation methodology. You know how to design a test, instrument it, and turn the results into a product decision.
• Experience with telephony integration: SIP, call transfers, IVR systems, or CCaaS platforms.
• Experience working directly with enterprise customers on technical products.
• Ability to context-switch between deep technical model evaluation and customer-facing product work without dropping either.

Even Better:

• Hands-on experience benchmarking across multiple ASR or TTS providers.
• Background in machine learning or audio/speech engineering, enough to hold your own in model architecture discussions.
• Industry expertise in verticals with high contact center volume: telecommunications, financial services, travel, healthcare.

There are only two hard problems in computer science: cache invalidation, naming things, and convincing an ERP that "Acme Corp." and "ACME Corporation" are the same vendor.

If that joke hurt a little, keep reading.

DistantJob is looking for a Senior .NET Integration Engineer to join one of our clients, a fintech company whose platform automates accounts payable, payments and financial operations for investment firms, family offices and fund administrators. Their customers rely on the platform to connect with the accounting systems they already use, so the integration layer is central to the product.

The role

You'll design, build and own the integrations that link the platform to ERP and accounting systems such as NetSuite, QuickBooks, Sage and Microsoft Dynamics. You'll work closely with a Staff Engineer and take real ownership, from scoping through production. You'll spend your time on:

• Building and improving REST and SOAP integrations that hold up against messy real-world customer setups

• Designing sync, mapping, validation and reconciliation workflows that keep data accurate between systems

• Handling partial failures, retries and eventual consistency, with idempotency and audit trails built in

• Improving performance and reliability, adding logging and alerting, and finding the root cause when an integration breaks

• Working with the onboarding and support teams to get customers connected and live

• Contributing to code reviews, documentation and engineering standards

This team is also actively adopting AI-assisted development with tools like Cursor, Claude Code and GitHub Copilot, so you'll have room to work that way.

What we're looking for

• 5+ years of software engineering with production systems

• Strong C# and .NET, including backend services and APIs

• Proven experience integrating with ERP, accounting or financial systems

• Solid knowledge of REST and SOAP, including authentication, error handling, retries and versioning

• Experience with data synchronization, transformation and reconciliation

• Strong SQL Server skills: query design, optimization and data modeling

• Experience with event-driven or message-based architectures

• Independence and clear communication with both engineers and non-technical stakeholders

Bonus points for:

• Hands-on NetSuite, QuickBooks, Sage or Dynamics integration work

• A background in fintech, payments, AP or fund administration

• Azure experience (Service Bus, Functions, API Management)

• SFTP, EDI or file-based integration patterns

• Python for scripting and tooling

• Multi-tenant SaaS experience

• Observability practices such as structured logging and tracing

• Daily use of AI coding tools

Details

• Location: Fully remote

• Schedule: US business hours, Central time preferred but can work in Eastern time

• Type: Full-time and long-term

• Time off: 10 paid vacation days and 8 paid national holidays per year

Why this one?

You'll own the integration layer of a growing platform, not just pick tickets off a backlog. The team collaborates closely, and the company is serious about its engineering standards.

Ready to make two systems agree on something? Apply and one of our recruiters will be in touch.

If you meet these qualifications and are ready to contribute your expertise to a dynamic team, we encourage you to apply!

jobs.title: Senior Inbound Product Manager, CRM Voice AI
jobs.description:
About the Team:

CRM Voice AI builds autonomous voice agents for customer service that resolve customer interactions end-to-end and drive significant value for the business. We're a team inside ServiceNow's CRM business unit, shipping production voice AI with enterprise customers today and scaling aggressively. Our agents run on a real-time streaming pipeline with best-in-class orchestration, integrated into the same platform where many of our customers already manage their front, middle, and back-office workflows. For those that don't, the voice agent is often the tip of the spear that brings them in. We compete directly against well-funded AI startups and CCaaS incumbents, and we're winning.

How We Work:

We work in pods - small, dedicated teams embedded with a single enterprise customer, building their voice agents from first call to self-sufficiency. A pod owns the full lifecycle: agent shadowing, conversation design, build, production go-live, monitoring and optimization and the handoff that makes the customer self-sufficient so the pod can move on to the next one. Each pod pairs forward-deployed engineers with a product manager who owns both the customer outcome and the product learning that comes from it.

Every PM on this team runs at least one pod directly and has visibility across others. You're in the customer's world - on their calls, in their systems, solving their problems - while simultaneously shaping what the product becomes. The learnings from your pods feed directly into the platform roadmap and into repeatable, productized assets that scale beyond any single customer.

What This Role Owns:

• You run two pods closely - hands-on through the full build lifecycle with two enterprise customers simultaneously, from agent shadowing through production go-live. You own the relationship with each customer’s team – setting the timelines and expectations, then delivering on them. You'll become one of the most experienced people in the company at knowing what it actually takes to ship a voice agent that works in the real world.
• For those pods, you and your team of FDEs own agent design, the build and evaluation.
• Your second area of focus is the tooling and intelligence layer that makes voice agents better and easier to build. This spans automated evaluation frameworks (how do we systematically measure whether a voice agent is good?), analytics (what happened on that call and why?), admin experience (how does a customer manage and improve their own agents?), and smarter agentic design patterns like deterministic procedures that give agents reliable behavior on structured tasks. You're building the infrastructure that lets this team, and eventually our customers, move faster and build better agents.

Why This and Not Somewhere Else:

This role puts you directly in front of enterprise customers running production voice AI from day one. You're not waiting to earn customer exposure - it's the job. The pod model means you'll accumulate more production voice AI experience in a year than most PMs get in several, across different industries, different contact center environments, and different conversation types. At the same time, the evaluation frameworks and agentic design patterns you build have reach well beyond your own pods. This team has a direct seat at the platform table, so the tooling you create shapes how ServiceNow thinks about voice agent quality at scale.

What You Bring:

• Experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI's potential impact on the function or industry.
• 5+ years of product management experience, or equivalent experience in a technical role such as engineering, solutions consulting, or technical program management where you owned product outcomes.
• Hands-on experience building and evaluating AI agents or conversational AI systems - conversation design, prompt engineering, testing and iteration against real user interactions.
• Comfort with data and evaluation. You think naturally about how to measure whether something is working and how to build systems that do it at scale.
• Experience working directly with customers or end users on technical products. You don't need enterprise sales experience, but you need to have been in the room where the work happens.
• Strong technical foundation. You can read code, understand API contracts, and hold your own with engineers on system design.
• An instinct for repeatable process. You see a problem solved once and immediately think about how to solve it for every customer.
• Experience with conversational AI, voice technology, or contact center operations.

Even Better:

• Familiarity with agentic AI design patterns and how to give an AI agent reliable, structured behavior alongside open-ended reasoning.
• Experience with telephony environments: SIP, CCaaS platforms, real-time media handling.

Join us at Sydecar, as we lead the charge in revolutionizing private investing.

Risk Management

What we're looking for

Bonus if you have

Our values are important to the way we live and work at Sydecar. They guide our priorities, behaviors and interactions.

Be Committed

As a team, we rise to meet challenges and recognize that we become stronger and develop character when facing adversity.

Be Excellent

We measure our success not just by what we achieve, but by how we achieve it—through integrity, creativity, elegance, and a commitment to continuous improvement. Excellence is not just doing things well—it's looking for ways to do them better.

Be Humble

Win Together

Winning requires that we give extra—sometimes winning calls for late nights or extra effort, and we show up for clients and each other with urgency and heart. While excellence is a journey, winning is a destination.

jobs.title: Director, Finance
jobs.location: Dallas, TX - Hybrid (3x in office/week); New York, NY - Hybrid (3x in office/week)
jobs.description:
About Lantern

Lantern is the specialty care platform connecting people with the best care when they need it most. By curating a Network of Excellence comprised of the nation's top specialists for surgery, cancer care, infusions and more, Lantern delivers excellent care with significant cost savings to employers and their workforces. Lantern also pairs members with a dedicated care team, including Care Advocates and nurses, for the entirety of their care journey, helping them get back to good health, back to their families and back to work. With convenient access to specialists nationwide, Lantern means quality care is within driving distance for most. Lantern is trusted by the nation's largest employers to deliver care to more than 6 million members across the country. Learn more about us at lanterncare.com.

Director, Finance

Lantern Care’s Finance & Strategy team is hiring a Director, Finance to lead the company’s annual budget planning process and rebuild its enterprise forecasting model. This is a build role: the budget process is maturing into a repeatable, top-down cycle, and the enterprise model needs structural rework, particularly on the revenue-forecasting side. The Director will own both, report to the VP, Finance & Strategy, and have a Sr. Analyst, Finance dedicated to supporting the work.

What you’ll own:

• Annual budget planning. Run Lantern’s long-range and annual budget process end to end, from kickoff through board presentation. Coordinate across Corporate Strategy and department finance leads, translate top-down revenue and margin targets into functional budgets and staffing plans, and keep the process on a defined timeline with clear deliverables at each stage.

• Enterprise model rebuild. Lead the rebuild of Lantern's enterprise forecasting model, with a focus on revenue forecasting. Rework how client-level performance drives near- and long-term forecasts, bring key business drivers (e.g., marketing activations) into the model explicitly, and establish a modeling foundation that supports enterprise decision-making and capital allocation.

• Forecasting rigor. Improve forecasting accuracy and process discipline across Finance & Strategy. Standardize methodology, reduce reliance on ad hoc corrections, and build frameworks the rest of the team can use without you in the room.

• Team leadership. Manage and develop team of two. Set priorities, review output, and make sure the model stays current between planning cycles.

• Executive communication. Present budget recommendations, model output, and forecasting methodology to the CFO and executive team. Anticipate the questions a sharp, technical executive audience will ask and come prepared with the underlying analysis.

What you’ll need:

• 8+ years in FP&A, corporate finance, or investment banking, including at least 2 years owning a budget or forecasting process end to end

• Advanced Excel modeling skills; comfortable building and rebuilding a three-statement model structure, not just updating one

• Experience translating ambiguous, top-down targets (revenue growth, margin) into bottoms-up functional plans

• Strong written and verbal communication; able to brief senior executives concisely and handle follow-up questions on the spot

• Direct management experience, or clear readiness for a first direct report

• Experience with financial software (e.g., NetSuite) and reporting tools (e.g., Power BI)

• Healthcare, healthcare services, or PE-backed company experience is a plus

• Experience using AI tooling (e.g., Claude) to optimize workflows a plus

Benefits

• Medical Insurance

• Dental Insurance

• Vision Insurance

• Short & Long Term Disability

• Life Insurance

• 401k with company match

• Paid Time Off

• Paid Parental Leave

Compensation: Base salary range: $200,000 - $230,000 + annual bonus (depends on location/level/relevant experience)

About You:

• You use LOGIC in your decision making and understand that progress is critical to making change. You focus on the execution of your content while balancing a fast-paced environment and you take the time to celebrate both the small & big wins.

• INCLUSION is a core tenant of your personal beliefs. A diverse and inclusive environment is incredibly important to you. You understand and desire to be a part of a diverse team with different experiences and perspectives & you cherish the differences in each individual that you interact with.

• You have the GRIT, drive and ambition to tackle big problems. Big problems require big ideas and a team that supports new ideas.

• You care deeply for your customers are driven to keep HUMANITY in all decisions. Your customers aren’t just the individuals using your product. They are the driving factor in your motivation to make a change.

• Integrity guides you in life. Focusing on the TRUTH vs. giving people the answers they want to hear.

• You thrive in a Team Environment. Collaboration is key in innovation and creating change.

These pillars of LIGHT are a reminder to our team that we are making a difference by providing guidance and support in navigating the often complex and confusing landscape of healthcare. We hope that through this LIGHT, individuals can find their way to the best care, resources, and support they need to get back to life.

If this sounds like you, we would love to connect to speak further about career opportunities at Lantern.

Please apply to our role & someone from our Talent Acquisition Team will reach out to help you navigate our interview process.

Lantern does not discriminate on the basis of race, sex, color, religion, age, national origin, marital status, disability, veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity or any other reason prohibited by law in provision of employment opportunities and benefits.

jobs.title: Operator II
jobs.description:
Position Purpose:

The Operator II is responsible for supporting the safe, reliable, and efficient operation of a reciprocating engine-based power generation facility consisting of multiple engine-generator units and associated balance-of-plant (BOP) systems. This role performs routine operational activities, monitors plant equipment, and assists in maintaining optimal plant performance while ensuring compliance with all safety, environmental, and operational requirements.

The Operator II works closely with the Shift Supervisor, Instrumentation & Electrical (I&E) Technicians, Maintenance Technicians, OEM representatives, contractors, and vendors to support plant availability, equipment reliability, commissioning activities, startup and shutdown operations, troubleshooting, and planned outages. This position requires strong mechanical aptitude, attention to detail, sound judgment, and a commitment to safe work practices in a high-reliability power generation environment.

Primary Duties/Responsibilities:

• Safely start, stop, operate, and monitor engine-generator packages and all associated auxiliary equipment in accordance with OEM specifications, plant procedures, and operating limits.
• Monitor plant equipment through the control system and field inspections to ensure safe and reliable operation.
• Adjust operating parameters and setpoints within approved OEM and plant guidelines to optimize performance, efficiency, and equipment reliability.
• Conduct routine equipment inspections and document operating conditions, equipment status, and abnormalities.
• Identify, troubleshoot, and report equipment malfunctions or abnormal operating conditions to the Shift Supervisor.
• Assist with plant startups, shutdowns, commissioning activities, and planned maintenance outages.
• Coordinate with Maintenance and I&E personnel to safely isolate equipment and return systems to service following maintenance activities.
• Complete operating logs, shift reports, inspections, and other required documentation accurately and in a timely manner.
• Participate in OEM and company training programs to develop a thorough understanding of plant systems, operating procedures, and equipment capabilities.
• Follow all company safety policies, environmental regulations, permit-to-work procedures, lockout/tagout (LOTO), confined space, and other safe work practices.
• Maintain high standards of housekeeping throughout the facility to promote a safe and organized work environment.
• Assist contractors, OEM representatives, and vendors while work is performed on site.
• Respond appropriately to plant alarms, emergency situations, and abnormal operating conditions.
• Participate in continuous improvement initiatives to enhance plant safety, reliability, and operational efficiency.
• Perform other duties as assigned by the Shift Supervisor or Plant Management.

Work Environment:

• Ability to work indoors and outdoors in varying weather conditions.
• Ability to work around high-voltage equipment, rotating machinery, elevated noise levels, and hot surfaces while following all applicable safety procedures.

Education/Experience/Background:

• High School Diploma/GED is required.
• Previous experience in industrial operations, manufacturing, utilities, oil and gas, or power generation is preferred but not required.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities:

• Basic understanding of mechanical equipment, pumps, compressors, engines, valves, and auxiliary systems.
• Ability to read and interpret operating procedures, equipment manuals, and technical documentation.
• Basic computer skills and ability to use plant monitoring and reporting systems.
• Strong communication, teamwork, and problem-solving skills.
• Commitment to maintaining a safe work environment.
• Ability to recognize abnormal equipment conditions and respond appropriately.
• Mechanical aptitude with the ability to learn complex plant systems.
• Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
• Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.
• Ability to prioritize tasks in a fast-paced operating environment.
• Willingness to work rotating shifts, weekends, holidays, overtime, and respond to emergency callouts as required.

Required Certification/Licenses/Training:

• Technical training or coursework in power generation, industrial operations, mechanical systems, or a related field preferred.

Physical Requirements:

• Ability to stand and walk for extended periods.
• Ability to climb stairs and ladders and work at elevated heights.
• Ability to lift up to 50 pounds.
• Ability to wear required personal protective equipment (PPE), including hard hat, safety glasses, hearing protection, gloves, and flame-resistant clothing.

Benefits: Veolia’s comprehensive benefits package includes paid time off policies, as well as health, dental, vision, life insurance, savings accounts, tuition reimbursement, paid volunteering and more. In addition, employees are also entitled to participate in an employer sponsored 401(k) plan, to save for retirement.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer! All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status.

jobs.title: Compensation Manager
jobs.description:
We are looking for a Compensation Manager to join our Rexel USA team in Dallas, TX! (Hybrid)

Summary:

Compensation Manager is responsible for designing, implementing, and managing compensation programs across multiple region and functional groups. This role ensures compensation practices are competitive, equitable, compliant, and aligned with business objectives. The Compensation Manager partners closely with HR, business leaders, and Finance to support talent attraction, retention, and performance through effective compensation strategies. This role plays a key part in mergers and acquisitions activity, including compensation due diligence, integration planning, job mapping, harmonization of pay programs, and transition support to ensure smooth integration of acquired businesses into the broader compensation framework.

What You'll Do:

• Lead the strategy, design, implementation, and governance of compensation programs across multiple regions and functional groups to ensure alignment with business priorities, market competitiveness, and internal equity.
• Manage broad-based compensation programs and frameworks that support organizational growth, workforce planning, talent attraction, retention, and performance outcomes.
• Oversee the development, administration, and evolution of salary structures, pay ranges, job architecture, leveling frameworks, and compensation guidelines to drive consistency and scalability across the organization.
• Partner with HR, Finance, and business leadership to develop compensation programs and strategies that support regional and functional business needs while aligning with broader company strategy.
• Provide strategic compensation consultation and recommendations for hiring, promotions, transfers, retention actions, reorganizations, market adjustments, and other employee pay decisions.
• Lead annual compensation cycles, including merit planning, salary review, incentive and bonus planning, budgeting support, modeling, and recommendations.
• Conduct market pricing, benchmarking, and competitive pay analysis using compensation surveys, internal data, and external labor market trends to ensure effective and informed pay decisions.
• Analyze compensation data and workforce trends to identify risks and opportunities related to pay equity, pay compression, market positioning, organizational consistency, and cost effectiveness.
• Monitor and evaluate internal equity across regions and functions, and recommend actions to support fair, consistent, and business-aligned compensation outcomes.
• Serve as a subject matter expert on compensation strategy, policy interpretation, program design, and complex pay issues, providing consultative support to HR and business leaders.
• Ensure compensation programs and practices comply with applicable federal, state, and local laws, regulations, and internal governance requirements, including FLSA and other pay-related compliance standards.
• Support the design and administration of base pay, short-term incentive, bonus, and other variable pay programs, ensuring programs are aligned to company objectives and operational needs.
• Lead job evaluation and benchmarking activities, including job matching, leveling, titling alignment, and organizational mapping across multiple business functions and regions.
• Prepare compensation analyses, dashboards, presentations, and business cases for HR leadership, Finance, and senior executives to support decision-making and program enhancements.
• Partner with regional and functional leaders to assess compensation implications of organizational design changes, workforce shifts, business growth, and talent strategy.
• Lead compensation-related work for mergers, acquisitions, integrations, and reorganizations, including due diligence, assessment of legacy pay programs, cost analysis, job and grade mapping, harmonization planning, and transition support.
• Collaborate with cross-functional partners during integration activities to evaluate financial impact, employee transition considerations, and alignment of compensation programs and practices.
• Drive continuous improvement of compensation processes, tools, systems, reporting, and documentation to improve efficiency, scalability, transparency, and user experience.
• Support participation in compensation surveys and maintain reliable market data sources to strengthen program design and decision support.
• Contribute to the development and maintenance of compensation policies, procedures, standards, and manager guidance materials to promote consistent application across all supported regions and functions.

Job Duties Disclaimer:

The information contained in this job description is intended to describe the essential job functions required of those assigned to this job. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, knowledge, skills, and abilities needed to perform the job. Please note that management retains the right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. The ability to competently perform all the essential duties of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation, demonstrate commitment to effective customer service delivery, integrity, and the ability to work productively as a member of a team or work group are basic requirements of all positions at Rexel USA.

What You'll Need

• 7+ years of progressive compensation experience, including support for large, complex, multi-region organizations.
• Significant experience in compensation, total rewards, HR consulting, or a related field.
• Experience managing compensation programs across multiple states, business units, and functions preferred.
• Experience managing compensation strategy, salary structures, job architecture, and market pricing.
• Strong experience supporting mergers and acquisitions, including compensation due diligence and post-close integration.
• Experience in base wage and salary administration, including market pricing jobs and working with salary bands, merit planning, and performance management programs.
• Experience in variable pay and sales compensation, including design, communication, implementation, and administration.
• Proficiency with compensation, incentive, commission, and HRIS systems; experience with Xactly, SuccessFactors, ADP, and PayFactors is a plus.
• Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including pivot tables, lookups, and complex data analysis.
• Relevant certifications (e.g., CCP, CBP, CPP, SHRM-CP or SHRM-SCP) are advantageousRelevant certifications such as CCP, CBP, CPP, SHRM-CP, or SHRM-SCP are preferred.
• High School or GED - Required
• 4 Year / Bachelor's Degree - Preferred

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

• Deep knowledge of compensation strategy, design, administration, and salary structure development.
• Expertise in job evaluation, job architecture, market benchmarking, and compensation planning.
• Knowledge of compensation compliance, pay governance, and applicable legislation, including FLSA.
• Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret data, assess trends and risks, and provide actionable recommendations.
• Ability to assess compensation trends, risks, and opportunities related to market competitiveness, internal equity, and program effectiveness.
• Proficiency in HRIS, compensation systems, survey platforms, and advanced Excel.
• Strong project management, organizational, problem-solving, and time management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, matrixed environment.
• Excellent interpersonal, written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate complex topics clearly to leaders and employees.
• Strong consulting, influencing, stakeholder management, and business acumen skills to balance strategic priorities with operational execution.
• High attention to detail, accuracy, and confidentiality when handling sensitive information.
• Ability to work collaboratively in a team-oriented environment while supporting business, integration, and compensation objectives.

Physical Demands:

jobs.description:
About Axiom:

Axiom is where legal teams go to find the right talent for everything from routine in-house tasks to complex outside counsel work. Too many legal departments are stuck having to choose between paying the high fees of their law firm, hiring full-time employees they don’t need, or turning to a low-cost agency that can’t meet their quality standards. At the same time, top lawyers want to work on challenging legal matters, but they want more control over how, when, and where they practice. Both are forced compromises that no one should have to make. Axiom shares and meets the higher standards of its clients and lawyers, with our “work smarter, adapt faster, go further” approach – connecting growing mid-market and Fortune 500 companies with the world’s deepest bench of experienced, specialized legal talent.

About the team:

The Business Operations team is the operational backbone of Axiom’s business, responsible for delivering consistent, scalable operating standards across all client engagements —from initial onboarding through the full engagement lifecycle.

The team plays a critical role in enabling Axiom’s success by ensuring operational excellence, and delivering on scalable processes and activities directly impacting revenue generation. The team supports internal stakeholders, legal talent, and clients globally, acting as a central hub for operational execution.

jobs.title: FL114: Senior Scientist, Therapeutics Engineering
jobs.description:
About FL114:

FL114 is an innovative, privately held biotechnology company developing our novel epigenetic editing platform to treat a variety of diseases through precise, tunable modification of gene expression. FL114 was founded by Flagship Pioneering, where companies such as Moderna Therapeutics (NASDAQ: MRNA) and Seres Therapeutics (NASDAQ: MCRB) were conceived and created.  With a strong emphasis on innovation and experimental execution, FL114 cultivates a highly dynamic and entrepreneurial environment.

About the Role:

FL114, Inc. is seeking a Scientist / Senior Scientist to join our integrated Platform as a key contributor in our Therapeutics Engineering efforts. The successful candidate will be an essential member of a close-knit team of experimental and computational scientists driving FL114’s product generation engine and supporting a broad set of therapeutic programs. We are looking for enthusiastic, detail-oriented, adaptive, and highly motivated individuals with a passion for bringing novel medicines to patients. Applicants should be comfortable working on a fast-paced, cross-functional scientific team.

Key Responsibilities:

· Independently conduct, optimize and proactively troubleshoot cellular screening assays in a wide range of primary and transformed cell lines.

· Expression and functional characterization of novel biologics modalities using various cell systems and techniques (cell-based assays, RNA/DNA/protein isolation and detection techniques, RT-qPCR, flow cytometry, etc.)

· Drive, pilot, and oversee development of a wide range of cutting-edge assays.

· Design, procurement, and maintenance of plasmids or other relevant materials for cell-based and cell-free assays.

· Identification and management of external partners (CROs, CMOs, etc).

Required Skills:

· Execute routine and advanced molecular biology techniques, including plasmid preparation, RT-qPCR, cloning, RNA/DNA extraction, gel electrophoresis, oligo pool work, etc.

· Culture and maintain a wide variety of mammalian cell lines, including transient and stable transfections. Develop cell lines as necessary.

· Analyze and interpret assay data, maintain accurate laboratory notebooks, and communicate results clearly in team meetings.

· Drive optimization and automation of screening protocols, including the use of liquid handling systems and plate readers.

· Experience developing DNA assets for molecular library design.

· Experience with gene delivery technologies (for example LNP, lentivirus, etc.).

· Exposure to CRISPR-based or other gene editing technologies.

· Experience with handling samples for NGS and for its interpretation.

· Familiarity with data analysis tools such as GraphPad Prism, Benchling, SnapGene, etc.

· Adaptive and detail-oriented with excellent time management and organizations skills.

· Exceptional teamwork and communication skills.

Required Qualifications:

· PhD in Cell or Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, or related disciplines with 2+ years of relevant experience in biotech or pharma.

· Strong background in cellular and molecular biology with hands-on experience in the development and optimization of cell-based assays and library screening assays.

· Extensive experience in gene design, vector construction, and protein expression.

· Possession of strong communication skills, both written and verbal, to clearly convey results and scientific data to senior leaders, teams and partners.

· Industry experience in drug discovery or pharmaceutical R&D preferred.

About Flagship

Flagship Pioneering is a scientific innovation engine that invents and builds companies that change the world. We bring together the greatest scientific minds with entrepreneurial company builders and assemble the capital to allow them to take courageous leaps in human health, sustainability, and beyond.

What sets Flagship apart is our ability to advance biotechnology by uniting life science innovation, company creation, and capital investment under one roof in a way that is largely without precedent. Our team of scientists, entrepreneurial leaders, and professional capital managers are each aligned around an institutionalized process that enables us to innovate and create breakthroughs for the benefit of people and planet.  Many of the companies Flagship has founded have addressed humanity’s most urgent challenges: vaccinating billions of people against COVID-19, curing intractable diseases, improving human health, preempting illness, and feeding the world by improving the resiliency and sustainability of agriculture.

Flagship has been recognized twice on FORTUNE’s “Change the World” list, an annual ranking of companies that have made a positive social and environmental impact through activities that are part of their core business strategies, and has been named four times to Fast Company’s annual list of the World’s Most Innovative Companies.

At Flagship, we recognize there is no perfect candidate. If you have some of the experience listed above but not all, please apply anyway. Experience comes in many forms, skills are transferable, and passion goes a long way. We are dedicated to building diverse and inclusive teams and look forward to learning more about your unique background.

Recruitment & Staffing Agencies: Flagship Pioneering and its affiliated Flagship Lab companies (collectively, “FSP”) do not accept unsolicited resumes from any source other than candidates. jobs.title: Lifecycle Marketing Lead - Insurance
jobs.description:
Lifecycle Marketing Lead, Insurance

About the Role

We are looking for an experienced Lifecycle Marketing Lead to own and evolve lifecycle marketing for our insurance business. This person will be responsible for developing customer communication strategies across the lifecycle, improving segmentation and personalization, identifying cross-sell opportunities, and ensuring our marketing technology and customer data are being used effectively.

This is a highly cross-functional role at the intersection of marketing, product, data, design, and technology. The ideal candidate combines strong lifecycle marketing expertise with enough technical fluency to work effectively with data and platform teams. They do not need to be a data scientist or engineer, but they should know how to ask the right questions, translate customer and business needs into data requirements, and turn those insights into effective marketing programs.

Experience in insurance or another complex, regulated consumer business is strongly preferred.

What You'll Do

Own Lifecycle Marketing for the Insurance Business

• Develop and execute lifecycle marketing strategies across key stages of the insurance customer journey, from prospect nurturing and conversion through onboarding, engagement, retention, and cross-sell.

• Identify opportunities to improve the relevance, timing, and effectiveness of customer communications.

• Build and optimize automated, trigger-based, and behaviorally driven marketing programs.

• Establish testing and optimization roadmaps to continuously improve customer engagement and business outcomes.

Drive Segmentation and Personalization

• Partner closely with Data Science and Analytics teams to develop and refine customer personas, audiences, and segmentation strategies.

• Help frame the right business and customer questions for the data team, translating marketing objectives into actionable data requirements.

• Use customer attributes, behaviors, product ownership, lifecycle stage, and other signals to improve targeting and personalization.

• Work with teams leveraging BI tools and other customer data sources to make relevant data accessible and actionable within marketing platforms.

• Develop a strong understanding of the customer data ecosystem, including both modern data sources and legacy environments, without needing to directly perform data engineering or advanced analytics.

Develop Cross-Sell Opportunities

• Identify opportunities to introduce customers to additional insurance products and relevant offerings throughout the customer lifecycle.

• Partner with Product, Data Science, and business teams to determine the right customer, product, message, and timing for cross-sell experiences.

• Build programs that balance business objectives with customer relevance and experience.

• Measure and optimize cross-sell journeys over time.

Work Cross-Functionally

• Build strong relationships across Marketing, Product, Data Science, Analytics, Engineering, Design, Compliance, and insurance business teams.

• Coordinate stakeholders to move complex lifecycle initiatives from strategy through execution.

• Clearly communicate requirements, priorities, tradeoffs, and results to both technical and non-technical audiences.

• Navigate the regulatory and operational considerations associated with communicating with insurance customers.

What We're Looking For

Required Qualifications

• Significant experience in lifecycle marketing, CRM, customer engagement, or marketing automation.

• Hands-on experience working with Braze, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, or a comparable enterprise lifecycle marketing platform.

• Demonstrated experience developing automated and personalized customer journeys.

• Strong understanding of customer segmentation, targeting, experimentation, and personalization.

• Experience partnering with Data Science, Analytics, or data engineering teams to turn marketing questions into actionable audiences and customer experiences.

• Ability to understand customer data models and data flows without needing to personally perform advanced analytics or data engineering.

• Experience partnering closely with Product teams in a digital or consumer-focused organization.

• Experience managing or directing the design and evolution of customer communications.

• Strong cross-functional project leadership and stakeholder management skills.

• Excellent communication skills, including the ability to bridge business, marketing, product, and technical teams.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience in insurance, financial services, or another highly regulated consumer industry.

• Experience developing cross-sell or multi-product customer strategies.

• Experience with Braze specifically.

• Familiarity with data environments and experience operating across evolving data architectures.

• Experience participating in or leading a CRM, marketing automation, or customer engagement platform migration.

• Experience working within a sophisticated customer data ecosystem spanning multiple products, platforms, and data sources.

What Success Looks Like

The successful candidate will develop a deep understanding of our insurance customers and create more relevant, personalized experiences throughout their relationship with us. They will help strengthen the connection between customer data, product experiences, and marketing communications; make it easier to activate meaningful customer segments; expand our lifecycle and cross-sell capabilities; and continue maturing the technology and processes that support our insurance marketing organization.

We are looking for candidates in the greater NYC area, as this position is Hybrid and will require an in-person presence a few days a week at our offices in Brooklyn, NY.

Salary: $140,000 - $160,000

This is a proposed Grade 12 individual-contributor role integrating hands-on clinical label design with independent clinical label review and approval accountabilities. The role has broad global scope, owns quality and timelines for assigned work, and has no direct reports.

Key Responsibilities:

• Review study protocols and related documentation to determine global clinical label requirements; partner with Clinical Supply Project Managers to evaluate label design options, supply needs, and implementation timelines.
• Create, design, critically review, and approve study-specific and global clinical label templates—including single-panel and booklet labels—within the validated label design system.
• Ensure label text, templates, and approvals comply with GMP/cGMP, applicable procedures, and global regulations for the United States, European Union, JAPAC, and other participating study countries.
• Independently obtain, document, and maintain required approvals from Regulatory Affairs, Quality Assurance, regional regulatory affiliates, and other designated stakeholders; resolve or escalate approval conflicts and compliance risks promptly.
• Maintain the global clinical label phrase library: approve new controlled phrases, conduct annual reviews, maintain phrase quality and consistency, and execute phrase library change management, including impact assessments and implementation planning.
• Maintain and update global and country-specific regulatory requirements in partnership with labeling leadership and regulatory stakeholders; assess requirements for new studies and booklet-label resupply.
• Coordinate with third-party label vendors on booklet label orders, proof specifications, print readiness, and quality expectations; support label printing, reading, inspection, and timely release activities as required.
• Review label and inventory impacts resulting from protocol, regulatory, or phrase changes; support inventory/resupply decisions and create destruction requests for expired or impacted inventory in accordance with procedures.
• Manage multiple simultaneous studies and competing priorities with independent judgment, accurate status communication, and accountability for on-time, right-first-time delivery.
• Collaborate cross-functionally to improve labeling processes, support team goals and operational initiatives, and identify, resolve, or appropriately escalate issues that may affect clinical supply or patient dosing continuity.

Minimum Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
• Demonstrated experience in clinical label design, clinical supply, pharmaceutical packaging, or a comparable regulated GxP environment; experience managing complex, global work independently.
• Working knowledge of GMP/cGMP and global clinical-labeling requirements, including US, EU, JAPAC, and other country-specific regulations; familiarity with CFR, EU Annex 13, and ICH principles.
• Ability to interpret clinical protocols, apply regulatory requirements, produce accurate documentation, and exercise sound independent judgment in review and approval decisions.
• Strong quality, analytical, organizational, project-management, communication, and issue-escalation skills; ability to manage simultaneous studies and timeline commitments.

Preferred Qualifications:

• 3–5+ years of clinical trial design, clinical labeling, packaging, or pharmaceutical manufacturing experience.
• Experience with validated label design systems, controlled phrase libraries, booklet labels, vendor proof review, inventory/resupply processes, and change management.
• Experience collaborating with Clinical Supply, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Packaging, and third-party manufacturing or labeling vendors.

jobs.description:
Vannevar builds AI systems for the Department of War's most consequential missions. We have 125 deployments across every branch and combatant command spanning our core platform and five distinct products. An an example of how we work, when major combat operations started with Iran, we fielded a new product supporting 24/7 operations and 9,000+ users in three months.

How we build is our advantage: we deploy forward with the people who own the mission. Our engineers, product team, and CTO deploy forward to the point of friction, including visiting units in Ukraine. We focus on embedding directly with operational units supporting great power competition with China, combat operations with Iran, and counter-narcotics missions.

About the role

Mission Leads are customer-facing owners of mission outcomes. You will lead engagements with government stakeholders to identify high-value mission problems, shape pilots and deployments, and turn demonstrated mission value into durable, funded programs.

This role blends mission credibility with strong execution and technical intuition. You will operate with high autonomy in ambiguous environments, translate mission needs into clear technical narratives, and coordinate across functional teams (Product, Engineering, Mission, Security, and Operations) to deliver and scale.

This is a customer-facing role required to be based on the East Coast (preferably Washington D.C.). Candidates should have experience in the SOF community or PSYOPs/IO community, and work will require time in secure or classified environments and frequent travel.

U.S. Persons status with at least a current Top Secret US DoD or IC clearance is required. This is a customer-facing role required to be based on the East Coast. Work will require time in secure or classified environments and periodic travel.

What you'll do

• Lead mission engagements. Build trusted relationships with operational, technical, and leadership stakeholders to understand mission needs, constraints, and success criteria.

• Translate mission problems into plans. Turn mission needs into clear problem statements, requirements, milestones, and measurable outcomes.

• Shape pilots and pathways to scale. Define objectives, timelines, and adoption plans that convert early wins into sustained programs.

• Communicate the “why” and the “how.” Create crisp technical narratives that map our agent-based capabilities to mission requirements and operational constraints.

• Run the operating cadence. Lead weekly customer syncs, internal standups, executive updates/QBRs, action-item tracking, and risk reviews, as applicable.

• Coordinate cross-functional delivery. Partner closely with Product and Engineering to ensure mission context is reflected in scope, tradeoffs, and delivery plans.

• Navigate program realities. Help stakeholders work through requirements development, budgeting cycles, contracting pathways, and coordination across organizations.

• Enable adoption. Coordinate onboarding, training, and customer success so the customer can use and sustain the capability.

• Maintain durable account knowledge. Keep high-signal documentation in Notion: stakeholders, org charts, use cases, timelines, deliverables, decisions, and lessons learned.

• Support expansion. Identify adjacent use cases and partner with Account teams where applicable.

What we're looking for

• 6+ years owning outcomes in complex customer environments (preferably in the SOF or PSYOPs/IO community)

• Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functionally without consistent guidance

• Strong written and verbal communication; able to synthesize ambiguity into clear plans and execution

• Ability to scope and articulate a solution credibly: connect mission problems to software capabilities and measurable outcomes

• Sufficient technical fluency to partner effectively with Product and Engineering and translate complex concepts into mission-relevant narratives

• Strong operational skills: planning, prioritization, stakeholder management, and follow-through

Nice to have

• Deep expertise in a specific mission or technical domain (e.g., cyber, information warfare, ISR, networks, operations, warfare systems/command and control)

jobs.title: Operations Lead - The Grove at Shrewsbury
jobs.description:
WHY JOIN ALO?

Mindful movement. It’s at the core of why we do what we do at ALO—it’s our calling. Because mindful movement in the studio leads to better living. It changes who yogis are off the mat, making their lives and their communities better. That’s the real meaning of studio-to-street: taking the consciousness from practice on the mat and putting it into practice in life.

OBJECTIVE

The Operations Lead is a member of the store leadership team and is responsible for driving and coaching to profitability and efficiency. The Operations Lead will work closely with Operations & Visual Managers in initiating, delegating work, and providing feedback to the team to achieve optimal results supporting total store operations. Duties require constant movement in and around the store, including the sales floor and back of house. When not actively assisting guests, this position takes initiative to perform other tasks, as needed, to keep store clean, safe, inviting and operating efficiently.

Operations Leader

• Lead & execute inventory management processes effectively with a focus on maximizing inventory accuracy and reducing shrink

• Investigate and root cause inventory accuracy issues, partnering with the General Manager to escalate process or system gaps

• Manage execution of key operational functions including shipment, receiving and processing, reverse transfers, sales floor recovery, intra-day sales floor replenishment, floor set updates, and supply management

• Champion strong visual standards for the sales floor

• Support a safe work environment and efficient operation through strong stockroom standards and processes

Business Leader

• Partner with Operations & Visual Managers to manage reporting, budgets, expenses, inventory control, supplies, vendor relationships, technology, and facilities to ensure maintained and maximized

• Demonstrate strong business acumen by leveraging metrics to support business-driving strategies

• Move dynamically on the retail floor to assess and fulfill the needs of the business, team and guests

People Leader

• Leads by example and inspires staff in daily operations and guest experience.

• Directly oversee the Operations Associates; responsible for recruitment and development of talent

• Use company performance tools to evaluate each operations associate and provide constant feedback to drive individual growth and improvement in partnership with the store leader

Flow Experience Leader

• Collaborate with Visual Lead to ensure cross-functional training, and Sales & Service Lead to ensure the business is well-executed

• Execute company-level operation-focused directives, projects and initiatives, in partnership with management team, to achieve goals & KPI’s

• Opens and closes the store in accordance with back of house (BOH) standards

OPERATIONS LEAD QUALIFICATIONS

• 2+ Years prior work experience in a client-centric, sales environment

• Proven leadership capabilities demonstrating excellent decision making

• Values feedback, receptive to receiving feedback and eager to provide

• Self-motivated with a desire to achieve results and excel individually, and as a team

• Excellent interpersonal and written communication skills

• Aligns with and embodies ALO’s Guiding Principles

• Requires constant movement in and around all areas of store

• Ability to lift, push, carry or otherwise move up to 50 pounds

• Ability to lift, bend, kneel, climb, crawl and/or twist, and safely climb up/down a ladder

• Ability to stand and move for an entire shift

OPERATIONS LEAD SCHEDULE

To build a balanced schedule that supports the needs of the business and our teams, we expect all full-time employees to be available for opening, closing and weekend shifts, which may be subject to change. All Employees are expected to be able to work from the week of and including “Black Friday” until the end of the holiday season, first week of January.

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, ALO does not discriminate against applicants or employees because of race, color, creed, religion, sex, national origin, veteran status, disability, age, citizenship, marital or domestic/civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression or because of any other status or condition protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

JUST SOME OF THE PERKS

• Generous ALO employee discount and free membership to ALO Wellness Club, with access to hundreds of streaming fitness and yoga classes with top instructors

• Competitive medical, dental and vision plan options, and enhanced additional benefits such as free virtual access to mental health providers and new parent support for employees and dependents

• 401K with company matching

• Monthly Store Incentives

• Clothing Allowance

The Company’s Lead base pay ranges from $19.00-23.00/ hour in Shrewsbury, NJ. Please also note, Leads are eligible to participate in the Company’s Monthly Store Incentive bonus program, which may result in bringing the total compensation to a higher range. Further, the range listed is just one component of the Company’s total rewards package for retail employees. Other rewards may include: clothing allowance, employee discount, 401K, competitive medical, dental, and vision plans, commuter benefits, and ALO Wellness Club.
