jobs.title: Senior Executive Assistant & Business Partner to the Global President
jobs.description:
About Us

At We., we've spent decades at the intersection of technology and humanity, bridging the gap between what businesses create and how people experience those creations. We've learned that beneath even the most unruly situations — whether it's a global crisis, an emerging technology, or a sweeping organizational change—lies a simple human need. That need could be for trust, connection, safety, or a sense of purpose. But it’s always there. And it is only by uncovering these truths that we can make real, meaningful progress.

Overview

The Senior Executive Assistant & Business Partner to the Global President serves as a highly trusted administrative, operational, and executive support partner responsible for maximizing the effectiveness, focus, and impact of both the Global President and the Office of the Global President. As the sole dedicated support resource for the Office of the Global President, the role combines high-touch executive administration with operational and executive coordination and requires exceptional judgment, discretion, agility, and executive presence. The Global President leads the North America Leadership Team across all agency sectors, Studio, and Global Marketing; is an owner of the Global Executive Team; and works in close partnership with the Global CEO. This individual owns the daily rhythm of support for the Global President, including intensive calendar management, scheduling across competing priorities and time zones, travel planning, meeting logistics, communications support, and real-time problem-solving while also helping coordinate priorities, facilitate alignment across a complex global stakeholder landscape, and ensure effective execution of commitments and follow-through, while anticipating needs before they surface and ensuring the Global President is prepared, informed, and positioned to lead at the highest level.

Success in this role requires a rare combination of administrative excellence, operational rigor, strategic thinking, and sound business judgment. The individual in this role manages the flow of information, decisions, logistics, and commitments surrounding the Global President, helping coordinate fast-moving priorities, facilitate timely action across teams, regions, and functions, and ensure exceptional day-to-day execution in support of a demanding global schedule.

At We. Communications, this role sits at the intersection of executive administration and strategic support within a collaborative, high-performing, globally connected organization. The Senior Executive Assistant & Business Partner to the Global President plays a critical role in enabling leadership through exceptional day-to-day execution, trusted partnership, and strong coordination across the North America Leadership Team, all agency sectors, Studio, Global Marketing, and key intersections with the Global Executive Team and the Office of the Global CEO. This role will report to the Chief of Agency Development.

Responsibilities

• Executive Support, Calendar Management, and Leadership Enablement Own intensive, high-volume calendar management for the Global President, balancing competing priorities, shifting demands, and global time zones with exceptional accuracy, responsiveness, and judgment. Manage daily scheduling, meeting coordination, and real-time adjustments to protect the Global President’s time, improve focus, and align the calendar with evolving business priorities. Serve as the primary gatekeeper for requests, issues, and opportunities requiring the Global President’s attention, applying sound judgment to prioritize, redirect, escalate, or resolve matters independently when appropriate. Independently assess competing demands and make day-to-day prioritization decisions on behalf of the Global President, exercising sound judgment within agreed-upon operating parameters. Anticipate scheduling conflicts, upcoming decisions, and key dependencies so the Global President is consistently prepared with the right context, materials, and stakeholders. Act as a trusted administrative and operational partner, offering proactive problem-solving, continuity, and support in a fast-moving, high-stakes environment. Maintain the highest level of confidentiality, discretion, professionalism, and responsiveness in all aspects of the role.

• Strategic Coordination and Executive Communications Manage the flow of information into and out of the Global President’s office, including correspondence, scheduling inputs, decision points, and follow-up actions, to ensure clarity, responsiveness, and strong day-to-day support. Draft, refine, and coordinate executive correspondence, internal messages, recognition notes, and other written communications on behalf of the Global President as appropriate. Monitor inboxes, incoming requests, and related communications to ensure timely action, informed decisions, and effective stakeholder coordination. Track key commitments, action items, and deliverables to drive follow-through and protect momentum on high-priority initiatives. Explore and apply AI-enabled tools and workflows to improve efficiency, streamline routine tasks, enhance executive support processes, and identify opportunities for smarter ways of working across the office.

• Stakeholder Management and Cross-Functional Partnership Build strong, trusted partnerships across the executive team, administrative community, key business functions, clients, vendors, and other internal and external stakeholders. Coordinate across the North America Leadership Team Sectors, Studio, Global Marketing, Business Development and other regions and functions to support the Global President’s priorities, facilitate alignment, and ensure smooth execution of commitments and meetings. Represent the Global President’s office with diplomacy, professionalism, and sound judgment, strengthening confidence in the office through every interaction. Maintain a tight working partnership with the Director of the Office of the Global CEO where priorities, meetings, and leadership coordination intersect.

• Meetings, Travel, Logistics, and Operational Excellence Lead detailed preparation for meetings by coordinating agendas, briefing materials, pre-reads, scheduling, logistics, and follow-up to ensure the Global President is consistently prepared and positioned for effective engagement. Manage complex global travel planning and itineraries with careful attention to scheduling, efficiency, business outcomes, executive preferences, contingency planning, and real-time adjustments. Oversee meeting and onsite logistics, technology readiness, hospitality, materials, and related support needs for executive meetings, events, recordings, and key leadership moments. Research, collect, and synthesize information as needed to conserve the Global President’s time and support informed decision-making. Create and maintain systems, trackers, and archives that improve continuity, organization, and visibility across the Global President’s office.

• Employee Engagement, Special Projects, and Office Stewardship Identify and support meaningful opportunities for the Global President to engage with employees, teams, and the broader organization in authentic and timely ways. Coordinate recognition, gifting, and special outreach on behalf of the Global President with strong attention to appropriateness, tone, quality, and follow-through. Support the coordination and execution of special projects, events, and initiatives sponsored by the Global President, ensuring strong execution and cross-functional coordination. Coordinate and help manage operational activities associated with the Office of the Global President, including project administration, vendor relationships, budget-related administration, executive events, and other office-sponsored initiatives. Bring a service-oriented, no-task-too-small approach while continuously identifying smarter, more effective ways to strengthen the office and support the Global President.

Candidate Profile

• Bachelor’s degree in business, communications, marketing, or a related field preferred; equivalent professional experience will also be considered.

• 8–12+ years of experience supporting C-suite or enterprise-level executives in complex, high-accountability environments.

• Deep experience providing high-touch executive administration, including intensive calendar management, complex scheduling, global travel coordination, meeting logistics, and day-to-day executive support.

• Demonstrated success balancing administrative excellence with strong business judgment, proactive problem-solving, and the ability to anticipate needs in a fast-moving executive environment.

• Exceptional communication skills, executive presence, and the ability to navigate sensitive interactions with diplomacy, professionalism, and confidence.

• Experience working across global teams or multiple time zones, with the ability to coordinate across complex enterprise leadership structures, broad stakeholder networks, and intersecting executive priorities with influence and discretion.

• Advanced proficiency with Microsoft 365 Office Suite including Copilot; comfort supporting executive technology needs is strongly preferred.

• Brings a strong sense of ownership, initiative, adaptability, and continuous improvement, with the responsiveness and resilience required to support a demanding global executive.

Role Environment and Expectations

• Location and flexibility: Positioned in or able to regularly support work in the Bellevue, WA area, with flexibility for in-office support, occasional travel, and availability outside standard business hours as business needs require.

• Operating environment: Excels in a fast-paced, high-visibility setting that calls for sound judgment, adaptability, responsiveness, and the ability to navigate shifting priorities with confidence and professionalism.

• Collaboration and influence: Builds strong, effective partnerships across leaders, colleagues, clients, and vendors, and works seamlessly across functions, levels, and geographies.

• Confidentiality and executive presence: Brings exceptional discretion, professionalism, and composure when managing sensitive business matters, executive communications, and high-visibility interactions.

• Leadership support: Demonstrates resilience, responsiveness, and professionalism in support of visible leadership moments, special events, and executive priorities.

• Operational support: Is comfortable providing occasional physical or logistical support associated with executive meetings, events, and travel.

jobs.title: Product Engagement Manager
jobs.location: Austin, Texas, United States; New York, New York, United States; Remote (US); San Francisco, California, United States
jobs.description:
About the role

Great products don’t stop at the interface. The messages we send, the moments we choose to reach someone, and how easy we make it to take the next step are all part of the experience.

We’re looking for a Product Engagement Manager to make those moments better across Thatch. You’ll dig into where members, employers, and brokers get stuck, figure out why, and build ways to help them move forward. That could mean a better lifecycle journey, a smarter trigger, a new way to reach someone, or a change to the product itself.

You’ll have the tools and ownership to move quickly: digging into data, building in Braze, testing ideas, and working with Product and Engineering when the problem needs a bigger solution.

What you will do

• Find where members, employers, and brokers are getting stuck and understand why.

• Build and test ways to improve engagement and conversion across email, SMS/RCS, transactional messaging, and in-product experiences.

• Own and improve the logic behind how we communicate with people, from targeting and triggers to sequencing, frequency, and personalization.

• Build new ways for Thatch to engage with people, including two-way messaging, RCS, personalization, and language preferences.

• Work with Product, Engineering, and Data when the right solution goes beyond messaging.

• Measure what works, learn from what doesn’t, and use both to decide what to build next.

What we're looking for

• 5+ years working in growth, product engagement, lifecycle/CRM, or a similar role.

• You’ve owned engagement or conversion metrics and can point to things you’ve shipped that moved them.

• You’re hands-on with Braze or a similar platform and comfortable building and testing journeys yourself.

• You’re comfortable using data to find problems, form a hypothesis, and measure whether your solution worked.

• You think like a product builder. You know when messaging can solve a problem and when the product itself needs to change.

Experience that stands out

• You’ve worked across several engagement surfaces, not just email.

• You can use SQL or analytics tools to answer your own questions.

• You’ve worked on complex customer journeys or products with multiple audiences.

• Experience in healthcare, benefits, fintech, or another regulated industry.

• You use AI as part of how you work.

• Unshakable optimism in the face of adversity.

How we work

• We give people ownership and trust them to make good decisions.

• We move quickly, learn from customers, and improve continuously.

• We solve hard problems together, regardless of team or title.

• We care more about building the right thing than following a perfect process.

What to expect

We aim to keep the process thoughtful, rigorous, and efficient. Most candidates complete it within three weeks. You can expect:

• An initial conversation with a recruiter.

• A conversation with the hiring manager, including a product review discussion.

• Conversations with product, engineering, and cross-functional teammates.

• A final conversation with executive leadership.

Estimated Compensation Range

$150,000—$195,000 USD

About Thatch

We’re a fully distributed early stage company using technology to change the way America does healthcare. We’re a happy, friendly, high-velocity team. You can read more on Thatch here.

The Sr. Practice Manager is responsible for managing complex clinical programs that require ongoing collaboration across business units, operations of one or more practice sites and supervising both clinical and administrative support staff.

Responsibilities:

• Manage the office’s front-line non-exempt staff, requiring interviewing, hiring, training, progressive discipline, dismissals, performance appraisals, and employee relations.
• Schedule staff and allocate resources across hours of operation to maximize patient access and satisfaction, provider productivity and efficiency, staff productivity, cost-savings, and operational efficiencies.
• Conduct supply purchasing via the Group’s on-line ordering and shopping list system within specified budget.
• Report monthly productivity results to providers and staff.

• Conduct timely and accurate cash management duties, including overseeing the collection of co-pays and patient balances and processing of clean super bill batches, in-house cash balances, and bank deposits to influence profitability.
• Serve as an active participant in corporate committees and task forces.
• Provide financial analysis to facilitate planning and cash flow management and review variance explanations.
• Communicate budget and variance information to professional staff.

• Identify and communicate priorities, timelines, and accountabilities to ensure efficient use of resources and to promote an open and productive work environment.
• Work with senior management to define performance goals for team and interface with staff to monitor progress, manage disciplinary issues and provide ongoing feedback.

Required:

• Bachelor’s Degree
• 5 years health care experience
• 2 years management experience
• Experience working within a clinical environment
• Outpatient setting experience
• Demonstrated organizational and leadership skills
• Excellent analytical skills.

Preferred:

• Master of Business Administration (MBA) or Master of Health Administration (MHA)
• Academic medical center experience

Northwestern Medicine is an equal opportunity employer (disability, VETS) and does not discriminate in hiring or employment on the basis of age, sex, race, color, religion, national origin, gender identity, veteran status, disability, sexual orientation or any other protected status.

Background Check

Northwestern Medicine conducts a background check that includes criminal history on newly hired team members and, at times, internal transfers. Sesame believes in a future where computers are lifelike - with the ability to see, hear, and collaborate with us in ways that feel natural and human. Integrating a complex sensing & computing system into a compact, attractive & functional wearable form factor requires significant mechanical expertise.  The PDE must drive or influence all aspects of development, including system architecture, mechanical form/architecture, thermal design/test, component & vendor selection/evaluation, prototyping roadmaps and execution, along with test & calibration.

The ideal candidate has experience owning wearable electronics design, strong prototyping skills, knowledge of materials and fabrication, good aesthetics, exposure to image sensor and battery integration, and the ability to collaborate across domains.

We are a small team working on very ambitious projects. In a fast-paced startup, everyone must be comfortable, collaborative, decisive, and able to achieve results with limited supervision.

jobs.description:
The Anesthesia Technician II reflects the mission, vision, and values of Northwestern Medicine, adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards.

The Anesthesia Technician II provides perioperative technical and clinical support to the members of the anesthesia team for all anesthesia procedures.

Seeking skilled and dedicated individuals who thrive in the fast-pace environment of the operating room. As an Anesthesia Technician, you will play a crucial role in the day-to-day operations of our healthcare facility, working closely alongside Anesthesia providers to ensure seamless procedures and patient care. You will receive comprehensive training to develop a strong foundation in anesthesia technology, ensuring the safety and comfort of patients undergoing surgical procedures. This position offers a unique opportunity to gain valuable experience and insight into the dynamic field of healthcare while making a meaningful impact on the lives of patients. If you are passionate about healthcare and eager to contribute your skills to a collaborative team, we want to hear from you!

Responsibilities:

• The Anesthesia Technician II works as a member of the surgical team, providing patient care under the direct supervision of a licensed anesthesia provider. Clinical responsibilities may include but are not limited to the following:Cell Saver-Blood Salvage (sets up and runs machine during surgery).Blood draws from patient lines (e.g. ACT-Clotting time, ABGs, venous samples, type & cross).Immediate emergency response - provide clinical and technical support.Assists with patient transfer (to and from the OR bed). Removes jewelry (e.g. rings/collaborating with circulating nurse re: OR protocol).Assists with patient positioning (especially arm placement and security).Places monitoring equipment (e.g. ECG leads, BP cuff, BIS Sensor, Pulse Oximeter probe).Assists with intubation, which may include the following at the direction of the anesthesiologist ensures all necessary equipment available & in working order, applies cricoid pressure, assists with fiberoptic intubations, provides jaw thrust, tongue pull, pulls stylet, inflates ET cuff, secures airway, or manually ventilate while the anesthesiologist confirms placement).Prepares patient for access line placement and invasive monitoring (e.g. preps patient, prepares sterile field / equipment, prepares arterial lines, central venous lines, additional peripheral vascular lines, cardiac catheters, femoral lines, unilateral ventilation, fiberoptic TEE probe management).Assists the licensed anesthesia provider in confirming patient identification.Verifies blood products per hospital policy (Blood Administration 5.91) with the hospital approved health care professional who will be transfusing the blood product.The Anesthesia Technician II does not transfuse any fluids including blood products.Under the direction of the licensed anesthesia provider assembles IV fluids for infusion, including blood products.The Anesthesia Technician II does not transfuse or monitor infused fluids.Provides patient security (e.g. during placement of spinal & epidural catheters, during intubation and extubation, during induction/intubation, and during extubation/recovery from anesthesia).Patient Transport.
• Anesthesia Equipment:Prepares, disinfects, and troubleshoots all anesthesia-related equipment and supplies for anesthetic procedures. This includes but is not limited to the following: Anesthesia Machines (e.g. Draeger Narkomed GS, Draeger Apollo, Datex-Ohmeda ADU, Draeger Mobile Machine and Tiro).Performs anesthesiology-related point-of-care testing.Monitors (e.g. GE Marquette Patient Monitor, Capnography and Gas monitors, Aspect BIS Monitor).Drug Infusion Pumps (e.g. Alaris, Hospira).Blood Infusion Equipment (e.g. Belmont).Hotline-Fluid warming equipment.TEE-Echo Probe.Intubation equipment, including fiberoptic bronchoscopes and video laryngoscopy.Gas cylinders.Breathing circuits.Assists with movement of equipment and supplies to support room turnover and readiness.Maintains appropriate inventory levels of supplies and equipment related to anesthesia care.
• Offsite:Provides clinical and technical support to anesthesia staff wherever needed in the institution (e.g. ICUs, IR, MRI, GI, CT, EP, ED).Serves as a resource for anesthesia to staff in other departments.
• Attend in-services for continuing education/maintenance of competency.
• Orients new staff to the Anesthesia Technician role.
• Additional responsibilities as assigned.
• The Anesthesia Technician II position is 24/7 coverage, and all positions are rotating to meet the needs of the department and hospital.

What we Offer:

• A supportive and collaborative work environment with a team dedicated to patient care and excellence.
• A pathway to gain direct, hands-on healthcare experience that is crucial for medical school and a career in medicine.
• Opportunities for professional growth and development within Northwestern Medicine, including workshops, seminars, and mentorship.
• AA/EOE.

Required:

• 1-2 years of technical healthcare experience
• Exhibit exceptional attention to detail and accuracy
• Ability to adapt quickly to changing priorities and work effectively under pressure.

• Display a positive attitude and willingness to collaborate with team members to achieve goals.

jobs.title: Director of Lifecycle & Retention
jobs.description:
About Chicago Public Media

Chicago Public Media is one of the nation’s largest local nonprofit news organizations. Home to WBEZ 91.5FM, the Chicago Sun-Times, and Vocalo. Chicago Public Media reaches more than 3.3 million people weekly across broadcast, print, and digital platforms. As a mission-driven organization, we aspire to be the most trusted news source Chicagoans turn to for understanding the people, events, and ideas shaping our community.

Chicago Public Media is a 100% community-funded newsroom powered by nearly 97,000 members whose support makes our journalism possible. This sustained community investment helped drive nationally recognized work in 2025, including 29 awards from esteemed organizations, including the Public Media Journalists Association, the Edward R. Murrow Awards, and the National Association of Black Journalists.

We believe independent journalism is essential to a healthy democracy and that access to objective, fact-based news is a right for every citizen. We serve the public interest by creating diverse content that informs and enriches our community, supported by a dedicated staff of approximately 250 professionals.

For more information, please see the Chicago Public Media Annual Report.

The Opportunity

The Director of Lifecycle & Retention leads Chicago Public Media’s enterprise lifecycle strategy across brands, platforms, and audience touchpoints.

This role is responsible for designing the systems, frameworks, and strategies that strengthen retention, loyalty, participation, and long-term supporter value following acquisition. The Director establishes the lifecycle architecture, audience segmentation, performance goals, and optimization priorities that guide onboarding, engagement, renewal, sustainer conversion, upgrades, reactivation, advocacy, and long-term relationship development.

The role partners closely with Product, Marketing, Insights, Development, Editorial, and the Membership team to translate audience behavior and supporter data into coordinated lifecycle strategies across WBEZ, the Chicago Sun-Times, Vocalo, and future platforms

General Responsibilities

Audience Journey Ownership
The Membership department operates through two interconnected engines: Growth & Acquisition and Lifecycle & Retention.

The Director of Lifecycle & Retention owns the strategic framework governing the post-acquisition relationship. This includes defining how supporter cohorts move through lifecycle stages, where retention risks and opportunities exist, and how programs and channels work together to strengthen long-term audience value.

The lifecycle framework includes:

• Onboarding & Early Member Experience

• Sustainer Conversion

• Renewal & Retention

• Upgrade & Philanthropic Development

• Reactivation

• Advocacy & Community Participation

The Director establishes the strategy, segmentation, performance goals, and optimization roadmap across these stages. Specialized team members retain ownership of individual membership programs, channels, and experiences operating within that framework.

Growth & Acquisition owns performance through the first financial transaction. Lifecycle & Retention assumes primary strategic accountability following that transaction, with both functions jointly defining and evaluating acquisition quality.

Core Area of Focus - Lifecycle & Retention
Design and continually improve a scalable lifecycle system that:

• Strengthens long-term supporter loyalty and retention

• Identifies and reduces preventable churn

• Increases sustainer conversion and long-term giving stability

• Expands lifetime value across supporter segments

• Uses behavioral, transactional, and engagement signals to improve lifecycle decision-making

• Creates pathways for deeper participation and philanthropic progression

• Connects membership programs, communications, and experiences within a unified relationship strategy

Success Metrics

• Retention and renewal performance

• Sustainer conversion growth

• Churn reduction across audience cohorts

• Upgrade, reactivation, and long-term revenue growth

• Lifetime value improvement

• Audience participation and engagement performance

• Lifecycle experimentation and optimization performance

• Long-term supporter loyalty and relationship health

Sustainable Relationship Philosophy

This role is responsible for strengthening long-term audience relationships through participation, trust, belonging, relevance, and ongoing engagement - not solely renewal transactions.  Success in this role will be measured not only by retention performance but by the organization’s ability to deepen supporter connection and build durable, long-term audience relationships over time.

Strategic Responsibilities

Lifecycle Strategy & Modeling

• Design and optimize lifecycle frameworks across brands, platforms, and audience segments

• Establish lifecycle stages, audience strategies, and performance expectations

• Develop retention, churn, and lifetime value models aligned with long-term growth goals

• Identify retention risks, lifecycle drop-off points, and opportunities for deeper engagement.

• Establish lifecycle KPIs, dashboards, and performance reporting frameworks

• Lead lifecycle performance analysis and strategic recalibration

Audience Intelligence & Optimization

• Develop lifecycle segmentation frameworks using transactional, behavioral, and engagement data

• Identify behavioral signals associated with retention, churn, conversion, upgrade potential, and long-term loyalty

• Define priority lifecycle cohorts and differentiated relationship strategies

• Establish testing standards and a lifecycle experimentation roadmap

• Translate performance insights into strategic recommendations for programs, communications, and audience experiences

Engagement & Loyalty Strategy

• Define engagement strategies that strengthen retention, participation, and long-term supporter value

• Identify the experiences and behaviors most strongly associated with loyalty and retention

• Establish audience priorities that inform member programs, benefits, communications, and experiences

• Partner with Product and audience teams to connect personalization, digital behavior, participation, and membership strategy

• Develop frameworks for measuring relationship health beyond financial transactions.

Retention & Revenue Strategy

• Establish retention strategy and performance goals across supporter segments

• Define strategic frameworks for sustainer conversion, renewal, upgrade, philanthropic progression, and reactivation

• Identify cohorts requiring differentiated retention strategies

• Evaluate retention economics and lifetime value across supporter segments

• Partner with membership program owners to translate lifecycle strategy into effective renewal, stewardship, upgrade, benefit, and engagement programs

• Lead recurring lifecycle and cohort performance reviews

Lifecycle Messaging Strategy

• Establish messaging frameworks for onboarding, stewardship, retention, upgrade, and reactivation

• Define audience objectives, segmentation priorities, behavioral triggers, and measurement expectations for lifecycle communications

• Ensure continuity between acquisition messaging and the long-term supporter experience

• Partner with channel and program owners to translate lifecycle strategy into effective email, direct mail, digital, event, and other audience experiences

Cross-Functional Leadership

• Lead lifecycle strategy across Product, Marketing, Insights, Editorial, Development, Revenue Operations, and technology teams

• Translate Membership priorities into cross-functional requirements for audience data, personalization, product experiences, measurement, and engagement

• Establish shared lifecycle goals and decision frameworks across teams whose work influences retention and supporter value

• Represent lifecycle and retention priorities in organizational planning and product development

Team & Operational Leadership

• Manage and develop team members responsible for specialized functions within Lifecycle & Retention

• Establish clear strategic priorities, decision rights, performance expectations, and accountability across lifecycle functions

• Ensure membership programs, communications, and engagement efforts operate within a unified lifecycle strategy while maintaining clear functional ownership

• Build team capabilities in lifecycle strategy, audience intelligence, experimentation, measurement, and optimization

• Identify capability, resource, technology, and process gaps that limit lifecycle performance

Qualifications

• Experience leading lifecycle, retention, subscription, membership, CRM, loyalty, or audience relationship strategy

• Demonstrated ability to design lifecycle frameworks across multiple audience segments, products, channels, or brands

• Strong understanding of retention strategy, cohort analysis, churn reduction, segmentation, and lifetime value optimization

• Experience translating behavioral, transactional, and engagement data into audience strategies and organizational decisions

• Experience establishing KPIs, performance frameworks, experimentation programs, and optimization roadmaps

• Experience leading complex cross-functional initiatives across Product, Marketing, Insights, Development, Editorial, technology, or comparable functions

• Ability to move between enterprise strategy, analytical insight, and implementation through specialized teams

• Experience building personalization, loyalty, engagement, or member experience strategies

• Strong people leadership, strategic communication, and organizational planning skills

• Demonstrated ability to build new capabilities, systems, or operating models rather than solely manage established programs

Compensation

The expected pay range for this position is $118,000 - $147,000 per ANNUM.

Chicago Public Media provides pay ranges representing its good faith estimate of what the organization reasonably expects to pay for a position.  The pay offered to a selected candidate will be determined based on factors such as (but not limited to the scope and responsibilities of the position, the qualifications of the selected candidate, departmental budget availability, internal equity, geographical location, and external market pay for comparable jobs.

Working at Chicago Public Media

At Chicago Public Media, we care deeply about our employees as we know attracting, developing, and growing talent is key to our success and enhancing our impact.

Our culture is one where collaboration, diversity of ideas, and innovation are encouraged.  We value colleagues who will enhance our culture by bringing new ideas, divergent experiences, and talents to our dynamic workplace.

At Chicago Public Media we believe dedication to a great workplace includes supporting our employees and their families. As a result, we provide a broad and generous benefits package for employees at hire and in the years to come.

Our benefits include a competitive salary and benefits package which includes medical, dental, vision, vacation, holidays, life insurance, disability coverage, retirement savings, and a commuter benefits plan.

Chicago Public Media is an Equal Opportunity Employer and we actively seek and welcome people from all backgrounds, orientations, and life experiences to join our team.

The essential functions described above are not all-inclusive and are not intended to create any contractual or other legal commitment. Chicago Public Media may change the content or format of this job at any time in its sole and exclusive discretion without notice.

jobs.title: Associate Creative Director, Copy (Remote Canada)
jobs.description:
THE ROLE

Directive is a revenue-first marketing consultancy built to serve B2B SaaS, enterprise technology, industrial, and commerce brands. We don't make things look good for its own sake. We build visual systems that hold up under the pressure of performance channels, complex professional services positioning, and a buying audience that starts with a CMO and ends with a CFO.



We are looking for an Associate Creative Director who will translate Moments that Matter into creative territories, messaging hypotheses, campaign concepts, headlines, CTAs, and copy direction that designers can execute against.  The Associate Creative Director will bring senior-level creative judgment to work that is fast-moving, digital-first, and tied directly to business outcomes. This person will not simply wait for polished briefs or execute one-off design requests. They will help shape the ask, identify stronger creative angles, and translate strategic inputs into assets that feel clear, compelling, and differentiated.  They will represent creative in strategic new-business and portfolio-sales opportunities, help build speculative and portfolio creative, and support Directive’s move toward campaign-style case studies that can drive account growth and new revenue.



This is an individual contributor role — no direct reports — but the work will be high-visibility and the standard will be high.  The ideal candidate is copywriting-led and campaign-minded. They should have enough executive presence to participate in client and leadership conversations, but remain hands-on enough to write copy, review briefs, develop messaging territories, and shape creative direction without needing a fully staffed creative team around them. They should understand performance creative as a system of hypotheses, tests, learnings, and scalable winners—not just brand execution or asset quality.



Success means helping Directive replace deliverable-based requests with campaign briefs grounded in business objectives, buyer insight, test variables, and success metrics. The ACD should raise the quality of creative thinking before work reaches production, improve how Directive communicates to technical and enterprise buyers, and create the foundation for a scalable performance creative practice.


WILL OWN

Campaign Strategy

The ACD owns the idea, message, and creative direction before production begins — and helps prove that better campaign thinking can create better performance, stronger pitches, and more creative revenue.

 - Support new-business and portfolio-sales opportunities with speculative creative, campaign narratives, and stronger creative presence in strategic pitches.

 - Create the foundation for Directive’s strategic creative approach.

 - Primary responsibility is creative direction, campaign concepting, messaging strategy, and performance copy direction.

 - Turns campaign and creative briefs into territories, concepts, hooks, headlines, CTAs, landing-page narrative direction, and message sequencing.

 - Partners with designers by giving them a strong concept and copy direction to execute against.

 - Builds the early proof points, examples, and campaign-style case studies needed to support future creative revenue growth.
   
   

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

30-day success signal: Internal teams understand why this role exists, what it owns, and how creative requests should start shifting from asset asks to campaign briefs.

 - Audited current creative requests, briefs, production workflows, pitch materials, and performance creative examples.

 - Met with Creative Production, Paid Media, Growth, Sales, Account leadership, and executive stakeholders to understand opportunities.

 - Defined what a “good” campaign brief needs to include before work enters production.

 - Created a first draft of the campaign creative brief template tied to Moments that Matter / Stratos.

 - Identified 2–3 priority use cases where the new model can prove value quickly, such as strategic account pitches, paid social campaigns, ABM campaigns, or portfolio-sales opportunities.

 - Produced at least one example of a stronger campaign territory or messaging direction from an existing work.
   
   

90-day success signal: Directive can point to live examples where creative strategy made the work sharper before production began, and stakeholders feel the new process is improving clarity, quality, and pitch readiness.

 - Run several real briefs through a campaign-level creative process: insight, hypothesis, concept, copy direction, production handoff, launch, and learning.

 - Developed creative territories, messaging angles, campaign copy, and testing recommendations for priority initiatives.

 - Supported at least one new-business, strategic account, or portfolio-sales opportunity with speculative or campaign-style creative.

 - Built a working partnership model with production designers so designers are executing against clearer concepts and copy direction.

 - Created early examples of campaign-style case studies or internal proof points.

 - Established a lightweight creative review rhythm focused on concept quality, message clarity, testability, and business relevance.

 - Begun defining the message/proof library and taxonomy needed for learning to compound across campaigns.

 - You have an established creative testing rhythm: hypothesis → variant → data → decision, repeatable without manual oversight.
   
   

QUALIFICATIONS

Experience & Portfolio

Creative Expertise

 - 4–6 years of professional creative experience, with a meaningful portion in an agency, professional services, or B2B marketing environment

 - A portfolio that shows range across brand work and performance creative — we need to see both a visual system you built and an ad campaign you designed that drove measurable results

 - Experience developing campaigns from concept through execution.

 - Ability to maintain and evolve brand standards across multiple channels.
   
   

Strategic and Business Skills

 - Understanding of creative strategy and storytelling.

 - Ability to translate ICP, positioning, personas, JTBD insights, proof points, objections, and funnel-stage context into creative hypotheses and campaign concepts.

 - Executive presence and confidence presenting creative strategy in new-business, portfolio-sales, client-facing, or leadership settings.

 - Strong understanding of performance creative, testing methodology, message iteration, pipeline influence, and revenue-oriented creative measurement.

 - Ability to partner effectively with production designers, paid media strategists, Account Directors, Growth, and Sales without needing to personally execute design production.

 - Comfort operating in ambiguity and helping shape the brief when the request is not fully formed.
   
   

Technical and Industry Knowledge

 - Digital marketing and social media

 - UX/UI design

 - Video and motion graphics

 - Content strategy

 - Creative software such as Adobe Creative Cloud

 - AI-assisted creative tools and emerging technologies
   
   

Tools — Required

 - Adobe Creative Suite — Illustrator, Photoshop, InDesign (expert level)

 - Adobe After Effects and Premiere Pro — proficient; you can produce and deliver without a separate editor

 - Figma — design systems, component libraries, collaborative handoff

 - Familiarity with A/B testing and CRO tools — Optimizely, Unbounce, Crazy Egg, or equivalent

 - Heavy reliance and comfortability with generative AI and a recommended tool-set day 1.
   
   

Tools — Preferred

 - Project management tools — Asana, or similar; you will work within an existing PM workflow

 - Familiarity with a marketing analytics stack — GA4, Looker, or similar; you can read a dashboard and extract creative implications independently
   
   

WHAT WE OFFER

 - 🏠 We have a set living wage at Directive; The annual base salary range for this position based in Canada is $115,000-$125,000 CAD. This salary range is an estimate, and the actual salary may vary based on Directive's compensation practices, job related skills, and depth of experience.
   
    

 - 🙏  Medical, dental, vision plans, disability, and life insurance coverage for you and your family that fit your lifestyle
   
   - Including a 100% employer-paid plan for you and a 50% employer contribution for your dependents

 - Benefits to Support the Whole Person:
   
   - 🧠  Mental - Access to certified therapists through Spring Health, membership to Headspace
   
   - 💪  Physical - Physical therapy through Omada, fertility support through Carrott, thousands of Aaptiv virtual workouts, complimentary One Medical membership for primary and virtual care
   
   - 🛫 Time Off - Unlimited PTO (2-week minimum), Paid Company Holidays, Your Birthday Off, End of Year Recharge (Closed December 24 - January 1), Paid Parental Leave
   
   - 💰 Financial - Traditional and Roth 401(k) with a 3% company match
   
   - 🌟  Bonus - Annual bonus based on tenure, which scales in total amount over time
     
     

WORK ENVIRONMENT

Directive is a remote-first company. This role operates 100% virtually from your home office. We collaborate through Zoom and Slack. You will need a reliable setup, high-speed internet, and a professional working environment capable of running Adobe Creative Suite and video production software without interruption.

We accommodate global candidates in markets where Directive has established business operations, including Canada, Mexico, and the UK. Current, permanent work authorization in that country is required. Due to the nature of this role, you must be able to remain stationary for extended periods, operate design and video software on Mac or PC, and observe and interpret written and verbal communication consistently. Reasonable accommodations are available for qualified individuals with disabilities — contact recruiting@directiveconsulting.com.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

At Directive, one of our core values is People First. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture in the digital landscape. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

jobs.description:
Who is Eleos Health?

The people who deliver care in our communities and homes do some of the most important work in healthcare. But too often, theyʼre asked to spend their time navigating paperwork, administrative burden, and problems they only discover after something has already gone wrong.

Eleos exists to change that.

Weʼre building the system of action for community-based care - helping behavioral health, hospice, home health, and other care teams spend less time reacting to problems and more time focused on the people they serve.

Powered by our Polaris AI, Eleos works alongside clinicians and their teams to understand whatʼs happening across care in real time and take action before issues become problems, reducing administrative burden, protecting revenue and compliance, and giving care teams more time and
capacity to deliver great care.

Our vision is a world where care teams can stay one step ahead, rather than constantly catching up. Weʼre helping shift an entire industry from reactive to proactive, and we need talented people to help us get there.

Our vision is a world where care teams can stay one step ahead, rather than constantly catching up. Weʼre helping shift an entire industry from reactive to proactive, and we need talented people to help us get there.

What’s the opportunity?

We are seeking a strategic, operationally rigorous Director of Partnerships & Business Development to build and lead Eleos’ partnerships function. Reporting to the Vice President of Growth, you will own partnership strategy and execution across our full partner portfolio, including state and regional behavioral health association partnerships, group purchasing organization (GPO) relationships, certification and credentialing body partnerships, white-label distribution partnerships, and GPO relationships supporting our expansion into home health and hospice. You will lead and develop a team of partnership managers, several of whom are already in place managing existing relationships, and you will be accountable for building the infrastructure this function needs to scale, including contract structures, Salesforce pipeline tracking, and partner ROI measurement. This is as much a build role as a leadership role: you’ll inherit a valuable network of relationships and help shape it into a more structured, measurable growth channel.

Who are you?

You are an operator who has built or significantly scaled a partnership, channel, or business development function before, ideally from an early or unstructured state, not only managed one that was already mature. You think in systems as much as relationships: you know how to structure a partner agreement, define what good partner performance looks like, and build the reporting that proves it. You have led people, and you are just as comfortable negotiating a contract directly as you are setting a multi-year vision for a partner ecosystem. You have navigated organizational complexity before, including absorbing an existing team member or relationship from another part of a business, and you know how to do that without disrupting the trust that has already been built. You are comfortable with ambiguity and energized by the opportunity to turn a loose collection of relationships into a real growth engine.

How will you contribute?

• You’ll own partnership strategy and roadmap across Eleos’ full partner portfolio, including behavioral health association and GPO partnerships, certification body relationships, white-label distribution partnerships, and home health and hospice GPO partnerships.

• You’ll build, formalize, and negotiate partnership agreements, including commercial terms, attribution methodology, and credit structures, replacing today’s informal arrangements with a consistent contract framework.

• You’ll recruit, manage, and develop a team of partnership managers, including integrating an existing team member and partner relationship transitioning in from another part of the business.

• You’ll implement Salesforce tracking and ROI measurement for partner-sourced pipeline across all verticals, where little to none currently exists.

• You’ll serve as the primary cross-functional connector between partnerships and sales leadership, Revenue Operations, marketing, product, and Customer Success, and represent Eleos externally with senior stakeholders at partner organizations, associations, and GPOs.

What does success look like?

• In your first 30 days: you will deliver a comprehensive assessment of the team and the state of the partnerships business, including the talent on the team, the health of existing partner agreements, and where tracking and reporting infrastructure is missing, along with preliminary recommendations for immediate changes.

• In your first 90 days: you will be executing against a clear vision for the team and the partnerships vertical, with performance expectations set for your team and early progress visible on contract structure, Salesforce tracking, and partner ROI measurement.

What qualifications and skills will help you to be successful?

• 5+ years of experience in business development, partnerships, or channel sales within healthcare or enterprise SaaS, including direct ownership of partnership strategy.

• Has built or significantly scaled a partnership or channel function from an early, unstructured state, not only managed one that was already mature.

• Demonstrated experience negotiating and structuring commercial partnership agreements, including revenue share, attribution, and contract terms.

• Prior people management experience, including leading a team through organizational change or integrating an existing team member or relationship into a new structure.

• Proven ability to build relationships with senior external stakeholders, such as C-suite executives, association leadership, or GPO contacts.

• Operationally minded, with direct experience implementing CRM tracking and ROI measurement where none previously existed.

• Comfortable operating with ambiguity and building process and infrastructure at startup pace.

• Ability to travel 25-50% of the time, depending on the business needs

Some nice-to-haves are:

• Understanding of the behavioral health, substance use, or home health and hospice provider markets.

• Familiarity with state association, certification body, or GPO partnership structures within healthcare.

• Experience with Salesforce or similar CRM platforms.

• Experience operating in an early-stage (Series A or B) startup environment.

• Background in healthcare RCM, patient engagement, or care management technology.

The determination of what a specific employee in this job classification is paid depends on several factors, including, but not limited to, prior employment history/job-related knowledge, qualifications and skills, length of service, and geographic location.

jobs.description:
About Lantern

Lantern is the specialty care platform connecting people with the best care when they need it most. By curating a Network of Excellence comprised of the nation's top specialists for surgery, cancer care, infusions and more, Lantern delivers excellent care with significant cost savings to employers and their workforces. Lantern also pairs members with a dedicated care team, including Care Advocates and nurses, for the entirety of their care journey, helping them get back to good health, back to their families and back to work. With convenient access to specialists nationwide, Lantern means quality care is within driving distance for most. Lantern is trusted by the nation's largest employers to deliver care to more than 6 million members across the country. Learn more about us at lanterncare.com.

Senior Analyst, Finance

Lantern Care’s Finance & Strategy team is hiring a Sr. Analyst, Finance to support annual budget planning and the rebuild of the company’s enterprise forecasting model, and to own the model’s ongoing maintenance once rebuilt. This role reports to the Director, Finance and is the person who keeps the enterprise model accurate and current between planning cycles.

What you’ll own:

• Enterprise model ownership. Own the enterprise forecasting model day to day: data updates, formula integrity, version control, and documentation. Support the Director, Finance on the model’s evolution over time, like applying new drivers (e.g., marketing activations), testing new model logic against actuals, and validating that updates hold up before they go live.

• Budget planning support. Support the annual budget process: build supporting schedules, engage with business leaders across the org, consolidate functional department inputs, and refine point of view on 2027+ operating profile of the business.

• Reporting. Build and automate reporting (monthly financial insights presentations, KPIs) to push knowledge into the rest of the business.

• Special projects. Build the underlying analysis (market sizing, cost-benefit, ROI) that informs leadership's go/no-go decisions on major product partnerships, operational enhancements, technology investments, and other key capital allocation trade-offs.

What you’ll need:

• 2-5 years in FP&A or a finance analyst role

• Strong Excel and financial modeling skills; ability to build a three-statement model

• High attention to detail while also considering the “so what” of the company’s core financial challenges

• Comfortable owning a recurring deliverable independently, with minimal oversight, once ramped

• Experience with financial software (e.g., NetSuite) and reporting tools (e.g., Power BI)

• Healthcare or healthcare services experience is a plus

• Experience using AI tooling (e.g., Claude) to optimize workflows a plus

Benefits

• Medical Insurance

• Dental Insurance

• Vision Insurance

• Short & Long Term Disability

• Life Insurance

• 401k with company match

• Paid Time Off

• Paid Parental Leave

Compensation: Base salary range: $90,000 - $105,000 + bonus (depends on location/level/relevant experience)

About You:

• You use LOGIC in your decision making and understand that progress is critical to making change. You focus on the execution of your content while balancing a fast-paced environment and you take the time to celebrate both the small & big wins.

• INCLUSION is a core tenant of your personal beliefs. A diverse and inclusive environment is incredibly important to you. You understand and desire to be a part of a diverse team with different experiences and perspectives & you cherish the differences in each individual that you interact with.

• You have the GRIT, drive and ambition to tackle big problems. Big problems require big ideas and a team that supports new ideas.

• You care deeply for your customers are driven to keep HUMANITY in all decisions. Your customers aren’t just the individuals using your product. They are the driving factor in your motivation to make a change.

• Integrity guides you in life. Focusing on the TRUTH vs. giving people the answers they want to hear.

• You thrive in a Team Environment. Collaboration is key in innovation and creating change.

These pillars of LIGHT are a reminder to our team that we are making a difference by providing guidance and support in navigating the often complex and confusing landscape of healthcare. We hope that through this LIGHT, individuals can find their way to the best care, resources, and support they need to get back to life.

If this sounds like you, we would love to connect to speak further about career opportunities at Lantern.

Please apply to our role & someone from our Talent Acquisition Team will reach out to help you navigate our interview process.

jobs.title: Economics and Strategy Advisory Consultant
jobs.description:
AECOM Advisory is seeking a dynamic Economics and Strategy Advisory Consultant to support our growing global Advisory business line. We are seeking talented management consultants to join AECOM Advisory who are mission-driven for the role of our clients in supporting economic, environmental and social vibrancy. We are recruiting for this role in the following metro areas: Boston, MA, New York, NY, Washington DC, Raleigh, NC,  Arlington, VA, Philadelphia, PA or Miami, FL.

Join AECOM’s Economics Advisory team to shape decisions on some of the issues that define our lifetime: inclusive growth, climate resilience, the energy transition, and the future of cities, through the real projects AECOM delivers with its clients every day. You will tackle strategic challenges such as translating net-zero ambitions into bankable investment cases, quantifying the socioeconomic value for large-scale investments in energy, water, transportation, and AI infrastructure, and assisting public sector clients in shaping public policy and planning for their key investment and policy priorities.

Building off AECOM’s considerable expertise in infrastructure design and implementation, AECOM Advisory is a trusted adviser to senior level clients and executive teams on their most pressing enterprise and strategic needs.

Our team of 400 staff globally comprises business and policy analysts, economists, commercial strategists, technologists, as well as human capital and change management practitioners. We help our clients develop their strategy, improve their operational performance, and integrate digital systems to generate value for their stakeholders and impact for their communities. We serve the full value chain of clients active in infrastructure, the built environment, and community vibrancy, including: national governments, regulatory entities, city agencies, utilities, transit agencies, infrastructure operators, private corporations, developers and investors. The successful candidate will employ economics methods and rigorous analysis to lead quantitative and qualitative approaches to develop and/or evaluate strategies that address policy, infrastructure investments, supply chain and social challenges.

We are a new category of consulting firm; one that builds off true operational and technical expertise of our broader platform to bring industry depth and capability-driven insight to the clients we serve.

Reporting directly to the Vice President of Economics and Strategy, the consultant will oversee daily operations, manage technical delivery, and help drive the systematic expansion of this strategic service area.

This role demands a blend of expertise in microeconomic analysis, specifically as it pertains to infrastructure, public policy, real estate, and project finance. It also requires consulting skills to offer strategic guidance to public entities, private companies, transportation authorities, and private asset operators and financing partners. The position involves effectively connecting upstream insights to AECOM's core business lines.

As an Economics and Strategy Advisory Consultant in AECOM Advisory’s US East Region, your day-to-day role will be to define, lead and manage multiple tasks within a workstream as part of a larger engagement.

The responsibilities include but not be limited to:

• Serve as the principal technical investigator on complex business cases, employing different methods of economic analysis, such as microeconomic modelling, econometric estimations and cost-benefit analyses (CBA), to analyze client problems.
• Conducting business modelling (market sizing, segmentation, penetration, adoption) and investment analysis by building custom discounted cash flow (DCF) models to calculate revenue, EBITDA, NPV, IRR, CAGR for client’s policies, projects and programs.
• Leveraging analytical and data visualization tools (e.g., ArcGIS, Costar, IMPLAN, REMI, Python, Tableau) to derive patterns, trends and insights from client and third-party datasets to inform client recommendations. The ability to code your own econometric models is a valuable asset
• Conducting stakeholder interviews, including with C-suite clients and senior management stakeholders.
• Outlining, supervising and providing quality control over analytical tasks assigned to junior team members.
• Creating highly polished executive-ready decks as you work, to build buy-in and convey emerging data-driven insights.
• Synthesizing multiple inputs into coherent insights across a variety of formats; slide decks, written narrative, playbooks, dashboards and toolkits.

In addition, you will also have the opportunity to contribute to business development, through:

• Solutions hypothesizing and economic and finance framework development to meet our clients’ needs.
• Technical writing and long-form narrative development.
• Creating pitch decks and defining AECOM Advisory’s value proposition.
• Bringing commercial acumen around client needs, budgetary requirements, researching client contexts.
• Supporting logistical and administrative processes to ensure risk management and compliance.

Minimum Requirements:

• Bachelor's Degree in Economics, Public Policy, Finance or quantitatively related degree + 4 years of experience as a professional economist and/or quantitatively inclined management consultant or related experience (e.g., previous roles in business, public policy, economics research, private equity, investment banking or corporate strategy experience); or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education and at least 2 years of Management Consulting or equivalent experience
• Experience in microeconomic modeling and econometrics, combined with strong numerical reasoning and quantitative business acumen.
• Experience with funding and financing strategies, including value capture.
• Experience in economic and fiscal impact analysis.
• Experience evaluating financial cashflows, particularly public finance.
• Experience in financial modeling to determine financial feasibility of infrastructure investments

Preferred Qualifications:

• Master’s degree in Economics, Public Policy, Finance, quantitatively inclined MBA, and/or related fields. PhD training combined with practical business-oriented experience would be a plus.
• 8+ years of experience as professional economist and/or quantitatively inclined management consultant.
• Experience in real estate portfolio optimization and real estate economics is a plus
• Sharp analytical, logical reasoning and structured problem-solving skills, employing abstraction techniques to solve ambiguous client problems, and ingest and parse out large volumes of client information.
• Strong commercial insight and willingness to have an informed point-of-view, grounded in an interest in enterprise challenges, its key economic and social rationale and impact, and developing understanding of client industries and their context.
• Curiosity about infrastructure challenges, our clients, their business, and the industries they operate in.
• Strong interpersonal skills, client-service mindset and ability to act as a trusted adviser to clients.
• Work in a high-tempo, high-context client-facing environment, with the ability to maintain poise, maturity and work well under pressure.
• Able to be self-directed, anticipatory and responsive to iterative feedback.
• Outstanding attention to detail.

jobs.title: Order Picker Operator - Warehouse lll
jobs.description:
Address: 10462 Hickory Hill Road Ashland, VA 23005

Shift: Monday through Friday 6 a.m. to 2:30 p.m./10:30 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. and 2:30 p.m. to 11:00 p.m. Sunday through Thursday 10:00 p.m. to 6:30 a.m.

Hourly Rate: $20.50

What's the Short Version?

The Warehouse Associate III follows internal procedures to unload/load incoming and outgoing trailers. While unloading, this role sorts, palletizes and moves product using powered equipment. This role uses a Radio Frequency (RF) unit in combination with Internal Operating systems to track product and perform departmental error resolution functions within High Jump.

What Will You Be Doing?

• Unload/load incoming and outgoing trailers, operating powered lift equipment to move product and materials as needed.

• Prepare orders by processing requests and supply orders; pulling materials; packing boxes; placing orders in delivery area.

• Generate reports to acquire data as needed to support error resolution functions in the receiving process.

• Support other functions of the Distribution Center as needed, including error resolution, inventory audits, customer service, and invoicing and tagging shipments.

• Responsible for checking out equipment and returning in same condition on a daily basis. Inspects assigned equipment daily at start of shift.

• Maintain safe, secure, and healthy warehouse environment by adhering to organization standards and policies, and to legal regulations; alerting others regarding potential concerns.

What Are We Looking For?

• High School Diploma or GED Preferred

• 4-6 years experience in a warehouse environment; loading and unloading trailers.

• 1-3 years experience operating a forklift or heavy equipment

• Complete and maintain SanMar’s Lift Operator Certification in compliance with OSHA guidelines.

• Demonstrates ability to follow directions and change priorities or job duties as business needs require; rotate to other production functions as needed.

• Strong attention to detail.

• Ability to learn Internal Operating System and operate Radio Frequency (RF) unit.

• Ability to work in fast-paced, high-volume environment while meeting deadlines.

• Able to work both independently and within a team.

• Demonstrated verbal and written communication skills.

• Comprehend verbal and written instructions.

• Mandatory overtime as required, which may include weekends.

What's Our Offer?

Paid Time Off: You`ll accrue paid time off on a weekly basis based on hours worked up to 112 hours per year to start. Employees also receive 8 paid holidays and 1 paid family day off.

Additional Benefits:

• Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision benefits

• 401k plan and matches $1 for $1 up to 4% of earnings, matched & vested at every pay cycle

• Life insurance

• Short/long-term disability coverage

• Paid maternity/paternity leave

• Pet insurance

What Should You Expect?

DC Warehouse (Equipment): While performing the duties of this job, the employee is constantly required to stand, walk, talk and hear. The employee frequently lifts and/or moves up to 60 pounds. The employee operates powered equipment requiring use of both hands as well as full range of motion of the neck, head and back. The employee is frequently required to reach with hands and arms, grasp and perform repetitive hand, wrist and arm motions. The employee is frequently required to climb stairs, kneel/squat, bend and carry. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus. Employee may be required to wear a headset covering one or both ears. Employee will be required to wear Personal protective equipment such as a Protective harness while operating equipment. Basic English literacy is required for operation of machines and necessary daily paperwork. Work environment is moderately noisy. The employee is occasionally required to work near conveyor systems. There is exposure to dust and changes in weather conditions. Work is performed under typical warehouse conditions. Potential hazards exist with regard to machinery such as forklifts, pallet jacks, mechanized systems, etc. Work environment is hectic and fast-paced.The employee is regularly exposed to ambient lighting and can be exposed to extreme heat and extreme cold including climates consistent with outside weather conditions.

jobs.title: Strategic Partnerships Manager
jobs.location: Austin, Texas, United States; New York, New York, United States; Remote (US); San Francisco, California, United States
jobs.description:
About the role

Thatch Market is growing, and so is the partner ecosystem behind it. We’re looking for a Strategic Partnerships Manager to own the partners already powering the Market and help decide who we bring in next.

You’ll manage and grow our existing partnerships, identify where the Market should expand, and source and close the partners that can get us there. You’ll build deep relationships with our partners and look for opportunities to expand what we can do together, both within the Market and across Thatch.

This is a high-ownership role with the opportunity to shape what Thatch Market becomes as we scale.

What you will do

• Own our partner ecosystem. Manage our portfolio of Market partners, from performance and ongoing relationships to renewals, growth opportunities, and offboarding.

• Figure out what’s next. Understand what our members need, identify gaps in the Market, and determine which partners and categories we should pursue.

• Bring great partners to Thatch. Source, pitch, negotiate, and close strategic healthcare and service partners.

• Build partnerships that make sense. Structure commercial models that work for Thatch and our partners, with a clear understanding of the economics and tradeoffs behind them.

• Make partnerships work in practice. Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Marketing, and other teams to launch new partnerships, solve problems, and make them successful over time.

What we're looking for

• 4+ years of experience in strategic partnerships, business development, or a similar role, ideally in technology.

• A track record of personally sourcing, negotiating, and closing strategic partnerships.

• Experience building and owning strong partner relationships after launch and growing them over time.

• Strong commercial judgment and comfort navigating deal structure, economics, and tradeoffs.

• The ability to see beyond the immediate deal and identify broader opportunities for a partnership.

• Strong cross-functional skills and the ability to move work forward across multiple teams.

Experience that stands out

• Experience in healthcare, benefits, fintech, or another complex industry.

• Experience building partnerships that are closely connected to a product or customer experience.

• Experience working closely with Product and Engineering to turn partner needs into scalable solutions.

• Unshakable optimism in the face of adversity.

How we work

• We give people ownership and trust them to make good decisions.

• We move quickly, learn from customers, and improve continuously.

• We solve hard problems together, regardless of team or title.

• We care more about building the right thing than following a perfect process.

What to expect

We aim to keep the process thoughtful, rigorous, and efficient. Most candidates complete it within three weeks. You can expect:

• An initial conversation with a recruiter.

• A conversation with the hiring manager to dig into your experience and the role.

• Conversations with teammates across business development, product, and engineering.

• A final conversation with executive leadership.

Estimated Compensation Range

$150,000—$210,000 USD

About Thatch

We’re a fully distributed early stage company using technology to change the way America does healthcare. We’re a happy, friendly, high-velocity team. You can read more on Thatch here.

jobs.title: Financial Analyst
jobs.description:
Role Overview

Reporting to the VP, Finance and Administration, the Financial Analyst supports the company’s financial planning, analysis, and reporting activities, providing accurate and timely financial insights to support business decision-making. Reporting to the Vice President of Finance and Administration, this role plays a key part in budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, variance analysis, and the development of financial models and management reporting.

The Financial Analyst partners with individuals across the organization to understand business performance, evaluate financial trends, monitor key performance indicators, and translate financial data into meaningful insights. This position requires strong analytical capabilities, attention to detail, financial acumen, and the ability to communicate financial information effectively to both finance and non-finance stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities

• Support the annual budgeting and periodic forecasting processes, including gathering assumptions, preparing financial models, consolidating inputs, and analyzing results.

• Prepare monthly budget-to-actual and period-over-period analyses.

• Analyze revenue, expenses, headcount, operating results, and other key financial and business metrics to identify trends, risks, opportunities, and areas requiring further review.

• Develop and maintain financial models, schedules, dashboards, and reports used to support financial planning and business decision-making.

• Partner with department leaders to review financial performance, understand variances, monitor spending, and support departmental planning and forecasting.

• Assist with the preparation and analysis of company-wide key performance indicators and management reporting.

• Perform ad hoc financial analysis and scenario modeling to evaluate business initiatives, investments, operational changes, and other strategic decisions.

• Support cash flow forecasting and other financial planning activities as needed.

• Assist in tracking sales bookings, renewals and contraction data.

• Support the Finance and Accounting teams with contract management.

• Monitor financial and operational data for accuracy and consistency and work with appropriate stakeholders to resolve data quality issues.

• Identify opportunities to improve financial reporting, forecasting, modeling, and analytical processes through increased efficiency, standardization, and automation.

• Support Finance leadership with presentations, analyses, and other materials for executive leadership and other key stakeholders.

• Maintain confidentiality and appropriately handle sensitive company and financial information.

• Perform other duties and special projects as assigned.

Competencies Required:

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to interpret financial data and identify trends and insights.

• High attention to detail and commitment to accuracy and data integrity.

• Strong business and financial acumen.

• Effective written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate financial information to non-finance stakeholders.

• Ability to collaborate effectively across departments and levels of the organization.

• Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.

• Sound judgment and discretion when handling confidential information.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

• Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field.

• 2–5 years of relevant experience in FP&A, corporate finance, financial analysis, accounting, or a related field.

• Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel and financial modeling.

• Experience with budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis, and financial reporting.

• Working knowledge of financial statements and fundamental accounting concepts.

• Experience with financial systems, ERP platforms (Netsuite), planning tools, and/or business intelligence applications.

• Experience in a SaaS, technology, or high-growth environment preferred.
